title.zh: 卷四百八十七 列傳第二百四十六 外國三 高麗
title.raw: 卷四百八十七 列傳第二百四十六 外國三 高麗 Volume 487 Biographies 246: Foreign States 3 - Goryeo

sentences.zh: 建隆三年十月，昭遣其廣評侍郎李興祐、副使李勵希、判官李彬等來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Jianlong, Zhao sent his Broad Evaluation Vice Commissioner Li Xingyou, Vice-envoy Li Lixi, Judge Li Bin, and others to come to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Jianlong (962), King Zhao of Goryeo sent his Broad Evaluation Vice Commissioner Li Xingyou, Vice-envoy Li Lixi, Judge Li Bin, and others to the Song court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年春，降制曰：「古先哲後，奄宅中區，曷嘗不同文軌于萬方，覃聲教于四海？

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, an edict was issued, saying: 'The ancient sages, predecessors and successors alike, have held the central domain—when have they not sought one script and one track for the myriad regions, diffusing their teaching to the four seas?
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year (963), the court issued an edict that read: 'From antiquity sage-kings past and present have ruled the central realm—when did they not seek a single culture and a single path for all lands, spreading their civilizing influence to the four seas?

sentences.zh: 顧予涼德，猥被鴻名，爰致賓王，宜優錫命。

translations.literal: Considering my meager virtue, I have undeservedly received the great title; now that a guest-king has come, he should be granted an excellent bestowal of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on my modest virtue and the great title I have undeservedly received, now that a tributary king has arrived, he deserves a generous grant of honors.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司、檢校太師、玄菟州都督、充大義軍使、高麗國王昭，日邊鐘粹，遼左推雄，習箕子之餘風，撫朱蒙之舊俗。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the Protocol of the Three Dukes, Acting Grand Preceptor, Commander of Xuantu Prefecture, Commissioner of the Dayi Army, King of Goryeo Zhao—refined by the sun's edge, acclaimed as hero in eastern Liao, versed in the lingering ways of Jizi, cherishing the old customs of Jumong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, King of Goryeo, Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes, Acting Grand Preceptor, Commander of Xuantu Prefecture, and Commissioner of the Dayi Army—a man of refined excellence from the eastern marches, hailed as a hero in Liaodong, steeped in the civilizing legacy of Jizi and faithful to the ancestral ways of Jumong.

sentences.zh: 而能占雲候海，奉贄充庭，言念傾輸，實深嘉尚。

translations.literal: Yet he can observe clouds and watch the sea, present tribute filling the court; thinking of his devoted submission, this is truly deeply admirable.
translations.idiomatic: He reads the heavens and watches the seas, brings tribute that fills our halls, and shows a wholehearted devotion that we deeply commend.

sentences.zh: 是用賜之懿號，疇以公田，載推柔遠之恩，式獎拱辰之志。

translations.literal: Therefore he is granted a fine title, enfeoffed with public fields, extending the grace of gentle treatment of the distant, thereby rewarding his resolve to bow toward the pole star.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore bestow on him a splendid title and grant him public fiefs, extending our policy of cherishing distant peoples and rewarding his steadfast loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ah!

sentences.zh: 來朝萬里，美愛戴之有孚。

translations.literal: Coming to court from ten thousand li, his beautiful devotion is sincere.
translations.idiomatic: He has journeyed ten thousand li to pay court—a devotion both admirable and sincere.

sentences.zh: 柔撫四封，庶混並之無外。

translations.literal: Gently pacify the four borders, so that merging may leave nothing outside.
translations.idiomatic: May you gently govern your four frontiers, until all are brought within and none remain outside.

sentences.zh: 永保東裔，聿承天休。

translations.literal: Forever preserve the eastern lands, and thereby receive Heaven's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Guard your eastern realm forever, and so receive Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 可加食邑七千戶，仍賜推誠順化保義功臣。」

translations.literal: He may be granted an additional fief of seven thousand households, and is further given the title Meritorious Minister Who Sincerely Submits and Pacifies while Guarding Righteousness.'
translations.idiomatic: He is granted an additional fief income of seven thousand households and the honorific title Meritorious Minister of Sincere Submission, Pacification, and Righteous Guardianship.'

sentences.zh: 其年九月，遣使時贊等來貢，涉海，值大風，船破，溺死者七十餘人，贊僅免，詔加勞恤。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, envoys led by Shi Zan came with tribute; crossing the sea they met a great wind, the ship was wrecked, and more than seventy drowned; Zan alone escaped, and an edict was issued to console and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: That September, envoys led by Shi Zan brought tribute. At sea they met a violent storm; their ship was wrecked and more than seventy men drowned. Zan alone survived, and the emperor issued an edict of consolation and relief.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，遣使以方物來獻，制加食邑，賜推誠順化守節保義功臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao, envoys were sent presenting local products; an edict increased his fief income and granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Sincerely Submits, Pacifies, Upholds Integrity, and Guards Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao (972), Goryeo sent envoys with regional goods. The court increased Zhao's fief income and granted him the title Meritorious Minister of Sincere Submission, Pacification, Integrity, and Righteous Guardianship.

sentences.zh: 進奉使內議侍郎徐熙加檢校兵部尚書，副使內奉卿崔鄴加檢校司農卿並兼御史大夫，判官廣評侍郎康禮試少府少監，錄事廣評員外郎劉隱加檢校尚書、金部郎中，皆厚禮遣之。

translations.literal: The tribute envoy, Internal Deliberation Vice Commissioner Xu Xi, was promoted to Acting Minister of War; the vice-envoy, Internal Attendant Director Cui Ye, to Acting Minister of Agriculture and concurrent Censor-in-Chief; the judge, Broad Evaluation Vice Commissioner Kang Li, was given a probationary appointment as Vice Director of the Palace Workshops; the recorder, Broad Evaluation Outside Gentleman Liu Yin, was promoted to Acting Director of the Secretariat and Gentleman of the Gold Bureau—all were sent off with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xi, the tribute envoy and Internal Deliberation Vice Commissioner, was promoted to Acting Minister of War; Cui Ye, the vice-envoy and Internal Attendant Director, to Acting Minister of Agriculture with concurrent appointment as Censor-in-Chief; Kang Li, the judge and Broad Evaluation Vice Commissioner, received a probationary post as Vice Director of the Palace Workshops; and Liu Yin, the recorder and Broad Evaluation Outside Gentleman, to Acting Director of the Secretariat and Gentleman of the Gold Bureau. All were dismissed with lavish honors.

sentences.zh: 昭卒，其子伷權領國事。

translations.literal: Zhao died, and his son Chou provisionally directed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao died, his son Chou assumed provisional control of the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 九年，伷遣使趙遵禮奉土貢，以父沒當承襲，來聽朝旨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Chou sent the envoy Zhao Zunli bearing local tribute, stating that with his father's death he ought to succeed and had come to await the court's decree.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (976), Chou sent Zhao Zunli with local tribute, explaining that with his father's death he was entitled to succeed and had come to seek the Song court's approval.

sentences.zh: 授伷檢校太保、玄菟州都督、大義軍使，封高麗國王。

translations.literal: Chou was appointed Acting Grand Guardian, Commander of Xuantu Prefecture, and Commissioner of the Dayi Army, and enfeoffed as King of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was appointed Acting Grand Guardian, Commander of Xuantu Prefecture, and Commissioner of the Dayi Army, and formally enfeoffed as King of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，加檢校太傅，改大義軍爲大順軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Chou was promoted to Acting Grand Tutor, and the Dayi Army was renamed the Dashun Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Chou was promoted to Acting Grand Tutor, and the Dayi Army was renamed the Dashun Army.

sentences.zh: 遣左司御副率於延超、司農寺丞徐昭文使其國。

translations.literal: The Left Bureau Vice Commander of the Imperial Guard Yu Yanchao and the Agriculture Directorate Assistant Director Xu Zhaowen were sent as envoys to his country.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Yu Yanchao, Vice Commander of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard, and Xu Zhaowen, Assistant Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, as envoys to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 伷遣國人金行成入就學於國子監。

translations.literal: Chou sent his subject Jin Xingcheng to enter study at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Chou sent a Goryeo subject, Jin Xingcheng, to study at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，遣其子元輔以良馬、方物、兵器來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, he sent his son Yuanfu with fine horses, local products, and weapons as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo (977), Chou sent his son Yuanfu with fine horses, regional goods, and weapons as tribute.

sentences.zh: 其年，行成擢進士第。

translations.literal: That year, Xingcheng was selected in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Jin Xingcheng passed the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 三年，又遣使貢方物、兵器，加伷檢校太師，以太子中允直舍人院張洎、著作郎直史館句中正爲使。

translations.literal: In the third year, envoys were again sent presenting local products and weapons; Chou was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor, and the Palace Attendant Zhang Ji and the Compilation Bureau Gentleman on duty at the Historiography Institute Gou Zhongzheng were made envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (978), Goryeo again sent tribute of regional goods and weapons. Chou was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor, and Zhang Ji, Palace Attendant of the Crown Prince's Household, and Gou Zhongzheng, Gentleman of the Compilation Bureau on duty at the Historiography Institute, were appointed envoys.

sentences.zh: 四年，復遣供奉官、閣門祗候王僎使其國。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Tribute Officer and Gate Ushers Attendant Wang Chen was again sent to his country.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (979), Wang Chen, a Tribute Officer and Gate Ushers Attendant, was again sent to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，再遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, envoys were again sent presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year (980), Goryeo again sent envoys with regional tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年，又遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, envoys again came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (981), envoys came again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年，伷卒，其弟治知國事，遣使金全奉金銀線罽錦袍褥、金銀飾刀劍弓矢、名馬、香藥來貢，且求襲位。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Chou died; his younger brother Zhi provisionally directed state affairs and sent the envoy Jin Quan presenting gold and silver thread brocade robes and bedding, gold- and silver-mounted swords, bows, and arrows, famous horses, and aromatics as tribute, and also requesting succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (982), Chou died and his younger brother Zhi took provisional charge of the realm. Zhi sent Jin Quan with gold and silver-thread brocade robes and bedding, ornamented swords, bows, and arrows, fine horses, and aromatics as tribute, and to request formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 授治檢校太保、玄菟州都督，充大順軍使，封高麗國王，以監察御史李巨源、《禮記》博士孔維奉使。

translations.literal: Zhi was appointed Acting Grand Guardian, Commander of Xuantu Prefecture, Commissioner of the Dashun Army, and enfeoffed as King of Goryeo; the Investigating Censor Li Juyuan and the Erudite of the Book of Rites Kong Wei were sent as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was appointed Acting Grand Guardian, Commander of Xuantu Prefecture, and Commissioner of the Dashun Army, and enfeoffed as King of Goryeo. Li Juyuan, Investigating Censor, and Kong Wei, Erudite of the Book of Rites, were dispatched as envoys.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，遣使韓遂齡以方物來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, the envoy Han Suiling was sent with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxi (984), Goryeo sent Han Suiling with regional goods as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年，加治檢校太傅，遣翰林侍書王著、侍讀呂文仲充使。

translations.literal: In the second year, Zhi was promoted to Acting Grand Tutor; the Hanlin Attendant Calligrapher Wang Zhu and Attendant Reader Lü Wenzhong were sent as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (985), Zhi was promoted to Acting Grand Tutor, and Wang Zhu, Hanlin Attendant Calligrapher, and Lü Wenzhong, Attendant Reader, were appointed envoys.

sentences.zh: 三年，出師北伐，以其國接契丹境，常爲所侵，遣監察御史韓國華齎詔諭之曰：「朕誕膺丕構，奄宅萬方，華夏蠻貊，罔不率俾。

translations.literal: In the third year, the army marched north on campaign; because his country bordered Khitan territory and was often raided by them, the Investigating Censor Han Guohua was sent bearing an edict to instruct him, saying: 'I have received the great foundation at birth and hold the myriad regions; Chinese and barbarian alike, none fail to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (986), the Song launched a northern campaign. Because Goryeo bordered Khitan territory and was often attacked, Investigating Censor Han Guohua was sent with an edict that read: 'Having received Heaven's great mandate, I rule the myriad realms; from the civilized center to the farthest barbarians, all submit without exception.

sentences.zh: 蠢茲北裔，侵敗王略，幽薊之地，中朝土疆，晉、漢多虞，夤緣盜據。

translations.literal: This stupid northern borderland has violated the royal plan; the lands of You and Ji are the central court's territory—through the troubles of Jin and Han they seized the opportunity to steal and occupy them.
translations.idiomatic: These foolish northern tribes have violated the imperial domain. You and Ji are lands of the central court; during the disorders of the Later Jin and Later Han they seized the chance to occupy them by force.

sentences.zh: 今國家照臨所及，書軌大同，豈使齊民陷諸獷俗？

translations.literal: Now wherever the state's radiance reaches, script and track are unified—how can we allow our common people to fall among savage customs?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the empire's light shines everywhere and culture and law are one, how can we leave our people subject to barbarian rule?

sentences.zh: 今已董齊師旅，殄滅妖氛。

translations.literal: We have now marshaled the armies and shall exterminate the evil atmosphere.
translations.idiomatic: We have assembled our armies to destroy this evil scourge.

sentences.zh: 惟王久慕華風，素懷明略，效忠純之節，撫禮義之邦。

translations.literal: Only the King has long admired Chinese culture and always possessed clear strategy, displaying pure loyalty and governing a land of ritual and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: You, O King, have long admired Chinese civilization and are known for wise strategy, pure loyalty, and governing a realm of ritual and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 而接彼邊疆，罹於蠆毒，舒泄積憤，其在茲乎！

translations.literal: Yet you border them and have suffered their venom—to release your long pent wrath, is this not the moment!
translations.idiomatic: You border their lands and have suffered their poison—surely this is the time to vent the wrath you have long borne!

sentences.zh: 可申戒師徒，迭相犄角，協比鄰國，同力蕩平。

translations.literal: You should warn your troops, take turns in pincer support, cooperate with neighboring states, and with united strength sweep them away.
translations.idiomatic: Warn your troops, coordinate pincer attacks, join with neighboring states, and together sweep the enemy away.

sentences.zh: 奮其一鼓之雄，戡比垂亡之寇，良時不再，王其圖之！

translations.literal: Rouse the valor of a single drum-stroke, subdue the nearly perishing foe—the good moment will not come again; O King, plan for it!
translations.idiomatic: Strike with one decisive blow, crush a foe already on the verge of collapse—the opportune moment will not return; plan accordingly, O King!

sentences.zh: 應俘獲生口、牛羊、財物、器械，並給賜本國將士，用申賞勸。」

translations.literal: Captives, cattle, goods, and weapons taken should all be granted to your country's officers and soldiers, to express reward and encouragement.'
translations.idiomatic: All captives, livestock, goods, and weapons taken shall be granted to your officers and soldiers as rewards and encouragement.'

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹伐女真國，路由高麗之界。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan attacked the Jurchen state, their route passing through Goryeo's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan had attacked the Jurchen state, marching through Goryeo territory.

sentences.zh: 女真意高麗誘導構禍，因貢馬來訴於朝，且言高麗與契丹結好，倚爲勢援，剽略其民，不復放還。

translations.literal: The Jurchen believed Goryeo had lured and engineered the disaster; they therefore presented tribute horses to plead at court, also saying that Goryeo had allied with the Khitan, relied on them as support, plundered Jurchen people, and did not release them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen believed Goryeo had instigated the attack. They sent tribute horses to plead at the Song court, charging that Goryeo had allied with the Khitan, relied on Khitan power, raided Jurchen communities, and refused to return those taken.

sentences.zh: 洎高麗使韓遂齡入貢，太宗因出女真所上告急木契以示遂齡，仍令歸白本國，還其所俘之民。

translations.literal: When the Goryeo envoy Han Suiling came with tribute, Taizong produced the urgent petition tablet submitted by the Jurchen to show Suiling, and also ordered him to return and inform his country to restore the people they had captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Suiling came with Goryeo tribute, Taizong showed him the urgent petition the Jurchen had submitted and ordered him to report back to his king to return the captives.

sentences.zh: 治聞之憂懼，及國華至，令人言于國華曰：

translations.literal: Zhi, hearing this, was anxious and afraid; when Guohua arrived, he had someone speak to Guohua, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, alarmed at this news, had someone convey the following to Guohua when he arrived:

sentences.zh: 前歲冬末，女真馳木契來告，稱契丹興兵入其封境，恐當道未知，宜豫爲之備。

translations.literal: At the end of winter last year, the Jurchen sent an urgent wooden tablet reporting that the Khitan had raised troops entering their borders, fearing our authorities did not know and that preparations should be made in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Late last winter the Jurchen sent an urgent dispatch reporting that Khitan troops had entered their territory. Fearing we might not know, they urged us to prepare in advance.

sentences.zh: 當道與女真雖爲鄰國，而路途遐遠，彼之情偽，素知之矣，貪而多詐，未之信也。

translations.literal: Our authorities and the Jurchen, though neighboring states, are separated by a very long route; we have long known their true and false reports—they are greedy and much given to deceit, and we did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Though we are neighbors of the Jurchen, the distance is great and we have long known their ways—they are greedy and deceitful—and we did not believe the report.

sentences.zh: 其後又遣人告曰，契丹兵騎已濟梅河。

translations.literal: Afterward they again sent someone reporting that Khitan cavalry had already crossed the Mei River.
translations.idiomatic: They later sent another message that Khitan cavalry had crossed the Mei River.

sentences.zh: 當道猶疑不實，未暇營救。

translations.literal: Our authorities still doubted it was true and had no leisure to mount a rescue.
translations.idiomatic: We still doubted the report and had no time to mount a rescue.

sentences.zh: 俄而契丹雲集，大擊女真，殺獲甚衆，餘族敗散逃遁，而契丹壓背追捕，及於當道西北德昌、德成、威化、光化之境，俘擒而去。

translations.literal: Suddenly Khitan forces gathered like clouds and struck the Jurchen heavily, killing and capturing many; the remainder were defeated and scattered in flight, while the Khitan pressed from behind in pursuit, reaching our northwestern districts of Dechang, Decheng, Weihua, and Guanghua, seizing captives and taking them away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Khitan forces gathered in strength and struck the Jurchen hard, killing and capturing many. The survivors fled in defeat while the Khitan pursued them into our northwestern districts of Dechang, Decheng, Weihua, and Guanghua, taking captives away.

sentences.zh: 時有契丹一騎至德米河北，大呼關城戍卒而告曰：「我契丹之騎也，女真寇我邊鄙，率以爲常，今則復仇已畢，整兵回矣。」

translations.literal: At the time a single Khitan rider came to the north of the Demi River, shouting loudly to the border-garrison troops of the pass city and announcing: 'I am Khitan cavalry; the Jurchen raid our borders as a constant practice—now our revenge is complete and we are withdrawing our troops.'
translations.idiomatic: A lone Khitan rider came to the north bank of the Demi River and shouted to the border garrison: 'We are Khitan horsemen. Jurchen raids on our borders are routine—but our revenge is done and we are withdrawing.'

sentences.zh: 當道雖聞師退，猶憂不測，乃以女真避兵來奔二千餘衆，資給而歸之。

translations.literal: Though our authorities heard the army had withdrawn, they still feared the unpredictable; there were more than two thousand Jurchen who had fled the fighting and come seeking refuge, and we supplied them and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Though we heard the army had withdrawn, we still feared further trouble. More than two thousand Jurchen who had fled the fighting sought refuge with us; we supplied them and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 女真又勸當道控梅河津要，築治城壘，以爲防遏之備，亦以爲然。

translations.literal: The Jurchen also urged our authorities to hold the strategic crossing of the Mei River and build fortifications as a defensive preparation, and this too was agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen also urged us to hold the strategic Mei River crossing and build fortifications for defense, and we agreed.

sentences.zh: 方令行視興功，不意女真潛師奄至，殺略吏民，驅掠丁壯，沒爲奴隸，轉徙他方。

translations.literal: We had just ordered an inspection for construction when unexpectedly Jurchen troops came secretly and suddenly, killing and plundering officials and people, driving off able-bodied men, enslaving them, and relocating them elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: We had just ordered a survey for construction when Jurchen troops struck by surprise, killing and plundering officials and civilians, seizing able-bodied men as slaves, and carrying them off.

sentences.zh: 以其歲貢中朝，不敢發兵報怨，豈期反相誣構，以惑聖聽。

translations.literal: Because they yearly send tribute to the central court, we did not dare raise troops to settle the score—who expected they would instead fabricate accusations to confuse the sage ear?
translations.idiomatic: Because they send annual tribute to the Song court, we dared not retaliate with troops—yet they have turned around to slander us and mislead Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 當道世稟正朔，踐修職貢，敢有二心，交通外國？

translations.literal: Our authorities for generations have received the imperial calendar and practiced tribute duties—would we dare have two hearts and communicate with foreign states?
translations.idiomatic: We have for generations acknowledged the imperial calendar and fulfilled tribute duties—would we dare harbor divided loyalty or deal secretly with foreign powers?

sentences.zh: 況契丹介居遼海之外，復有大梅、小梅二河之阻，女真、渤海本無定居，從何徑路，以通往復？

translations.literal: Moreover the Khitan lie beyond the Liao Sea, with the Great Mei and Little Mei rivers as further barriers; the Jurchen and Bohai originally had no fixed settlements—by what route could there be coming and going?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Khitan lie beyond the Liao Sea, blocked further by the Great and Little Mei rivers. The Jurchen and Bohai have no fixed settlements—what path could allow constant traffic between us and the Khitan?

sentences.zh: 橫罹讒謗，憤氣填膺，日月至明，諒垂昭鑒。

translations.literal: Having suffered slander unjustly, indignation fills the breast; sun and moon shine bright—we trust Your clear discernment.
translations.idiomatic: We have been slandered without cause and rage fills our hearts—but sun and moon see all, and we trust Your Majesty's clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 間者，女真逃難之衆，罔不存恤，亦有授以官秩，尚在當國，其職位高者有勿屈尼於、舟阝元、尹能達、舟阝老正、衛迦耶夫等十數人。

translations.literal: Recently, among Jurchen refugees none have gone without care; some have even been granted official rank and remain in our country—among those of high position are more than ten, including Wuju Niyu, Ye Yuan, Yin Nengda, Ye Laozheng, Wei Jiayefu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Of late we have sheltered every Jurchen refugee who fled here; some even hold official rank in our realm. More than ten of high standing remain with us, including Wuju Niyu, Ye Yuan, Yin Nengda, Ye Laozheng, Wei Jiayefu, and others.

sentences.zh: 欲望召赴京闕，與當道入貢之使庭辯其事，則丹石之誠，庶幾昭雪。

translations.literal: We desire that they be summoned to the capital to debate the matter in court with our tribute envoy, so that our cinnabar-and-stone sincerity may perhaps be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that they be summoned to the capital to argue the case in open court alongside our tribute envoy, so that our steadfast loyalty may be vindicated.

sentences.zh: 國華諾之，乃命發兵西會。

translations.literal: Guohua agreed, and then ordered troops to be sent to join in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Guohua agreed and ordered Goryeo to send troops west to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 治遷延未即奉詔，國華屢督之，得報發兵而還，具錄女真之事以奏焉。

translations.literal: Zhi delayed and did not immediately obey the edict; Guohua repeatedly pressed him, received word that troops had been sent, and returned, recording the Jurchen affair in full and memorializing it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi delayed obeying the edict. Guohua pressed him repeatedly until word came that troops had been dispatched, then returned and memorialized the full account of the Jurchen affair.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣使朝貢，又遣本國學生崔罕、王彬詣國子監肄業。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, envoys were sent to court with tribute, and native students Cui Han and Wang Bin were also sent to pursue studies at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Goryeo sent tribute envoys to court and dispatched students Cui Han and Wang Bin to study at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，加治檢校太尉，以考功員外郎兼侍御史知雜呂端、起居舍人呂祐之爲使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong, Zhi was promoted to Acting Grand Commandant; the Merit Evaluation Outside Gentleman and Concurrent Investigating Censor in Charge of Miscellaneous Matters Lü Duan and the Attendance Gentleman Lü Youzhi were made envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duangong (988), Zhi was promoted to Acting Grand Commandant. Lü Duan, Outside Gentleman of the Merit Evaluation Bureau and Concurrent Investigating Censor in Charge of Miscellaneous Affairs, and Lü Youzhi, Attendance Gentleman, were appointed envoys.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣使來貢，詔其使選官侍郎韓藺卿、副使兵官郎中魏德柔並授金紫光祿大夫，判官少府丞李光授檢校水部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year, envoys came with tribute; an edict granted the envoy, Selection Office Vice Commissioner Han Linqing, and the vice-envoy, Military Affairs Bureau Director Wei Derou, both the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and the judge, Palace Workshops Assistant Director Li Guang, Acting Outside Gentleman of the Water Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (989), envoys came with tribute. The court granted Han Linqing, the envoy and Selection Office Vice Commissioner, and Wei Derou, the vice-envoy and Military Affairs Bureau Director, the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Li Guang, the judge and Palace Workshops Assistant Director, Acting Outside Gentleman of the Water Bureau.

sentences.zh: 先是，治遣僧如可齎表來覲，請《大藏經》，至是賜之，仍賜如可紫衣，令同歸本國。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhi had sent the monk Ruke bearing a memorial to attend court and request the Great Canon; at this time it was granted, and Ruke was also given purple robes and ordered to return together to his country.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhi had sent the monk Ruke with a memorial to court requesting the Buddhist canon. It was now granted, Ruke was given purple robes, and he was sent home with the envoys.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年三月，詔加治食邑千戶，遣戶部郎中柴成務、兵部員外郎直史館趙化成往使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Chunhua, an edict increased Zhi's fief by one thousand households and sent the Revenue Bureau Director Chai Chengwu and the War Bureau Outside Gentleman on duty at the Historiography Institute Zhao Huacheng as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Chunhua (990), the court increased Zhi's fief by one thousand households and dispatched Chai Chengwu, Director of the Revenue Bureau, and Zhao Huacheng, Outside Gentleman of the War Bureau on duty at the Historiography Institute, as envoys.

sentences.zh: 其國俗信陰陽鬼神之事，頗多拘忌，每朝廷使至，必擇良月吉辰，方具禮受詔。

translations.literal: Their country's custom believes in yin-yang and ghost-and-spirit matters, with many taboos; whenever a court envoy arrived, they had to choose an auspicious month and day before performing the rites to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo custom placed great faith in yin-yang lore and spirits, with many taboos. Whenever a Song envoy arrived, the king would wait for an auspicious day before holding the ceremony to receive the imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 成務在館逾月，乃遺書於治曰：「王奕葉藩輔，尊獎王室，凡行大慶，首被徽章。

translations.literal: Chengwu remained in the guesthouse more than a month, then sent a letter to Zhi, saying: 'The King for generations has been a feudal assistant, honoring and rewarding the royal house; whenever great celebrations are held, you are first granted insignia.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month in the guesthouse, Chengwu wrote to Zhi: 'Your house has for generations served as a feudal ally, honoring the throne. On every great occasion you are the first to receive imperial honors.

sentences.zh: 今國家特馳信使，以申殊寵，非止曆川塗之綿邈，亦復蹈溟海之艱危，皇朝眷遇，斯亦隆矣。

translations.literal: Now the state has specially dispatched envoys to express exceptional favor—not only traversing the vast distance of land routes, but also braving the perils of the sea; the imperial court's gracious treatment is indeed lofty.
translations.idiomatic: The court has now sent envoys expressly to show you special favor—not only crossing vast distances by land, but braving the dangers of the sea. The dynasty's regard for you could hardly be greater.

sentences.zh: 而乃牽於禁忌，泥于卜數，眩惑日者之浮說，稽緩天子之命書。

translations.literal: Yet you are bound by taboos, mired in divination numbers, dazzled by the empty talk of day-selectors, and delay the Son of Heaven's command document.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are held back by taboos, bogged down in divination, misled by astrologers' empty talk, and keep delaying the Son of Heaven's edict.

sentences.zh: 惟典冊之垂文，非卜祝之能曉，是以《書》稱上日，不推六甲之元辰；

translations.literal: Only the canonical texts' handed-down writings are not what diviners and prayer-officers can understand; thus the Documents speaks of 'the superior day' without calculating the jiazi cycle's origin hours;
translations.idiomatic: Canonical texts, not diviners, set the standard. The Documents speaks of choosing 'the superior day' without calculating the sexagenary cycle;

sentences.zh: 《禮》載仲冬，但取一陽之嘉會。

translations.literal: the Rites records mid-winter, taking only the auspicious gathering of the single yang.
translations.idiomatic: and the Rites records mid-winter ceremonies, taking only the auspicious moment when yang first returns.

sentences.zh: 粲然古訓，足以明稽，所宜改圖，速拜君賜。

translations.literal: Brilliant are the ancient instructions, sufficient to clarify what is to be examined; you should change your plan and quickly perform obeisance to receive the ruler's grant.
translations.idiomatic: These ancient teachings are clear enough. You should change course and promptly receive the Son of Heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 儻鳳綍無滯，克彰拱極之誠；

translations.literal: If the phoenix edict is not delayed, you can display your sincerity of bowing toward the pole;
translations.idiomatic: If you do not delay the imperial edict, you will show your loyalty to the throne;

sentences.zh: 則龍節有輝，免貽辱命之責。

translations.literal: then the dragon tally will have its luster, and you will avoid bringing the blame of disgracing the mission.
translations.idiomatic: then our mission will shine, and you will spare us the disgrace of failing our charge.

sentences.zh: 謹以誠告，王其聽之。」

translations.literal: I respectfully offer this sincere counsel—O King, heed it.'
translations.idiomatic: I offer this sincere counsel—please heed it, O King.'

sentences.zh: 治覽書慚懼，遣人致謝焉。

translations.literal: Zhi, reading the letter, was ashamed and afraid, and sent someone to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, reading the letter, was ashamed and alarmed, and sent someone to apologize.

sentences.zh: 會霖雨不止，仍以俟霽爲請。

translations.literal: It happened that heavy rain did not cease, and he again asked to wait for clear weather.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains continued, and he again asked to wait for clear skies.

sentences.zh: 成務復遺書以責之，治翌日乃出拜命。

translations.literal: Chengwu again sent a letter reproaching him, and the next day Zhi came out to perform obeisance and receive the command.
translations.idiomatic: Chengwu wrote again to rebuke him, and the next day Zhi came out to receive the edict.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣使韓彥恭來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year, the envoy Han Yangong was sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (991), Goryeo sent Han Yangong with tribute.

sentences.zh: 彥恭表述治意，求印佛經，詔以《藏經》並御制《秘藏詮》、《逍遙詠》、《蓮華心輪》賜之。

translations.literal: Yangong conveyed Zhi's intent, requesting printed Buddhist scriptures; an edict granted the Canon together with imperial compositions Secret Canon Exegesis, Roaming Chants, and Lotus Heart Wheel.
translations.idiomatic: Yangong conveyed Zhi's request for printed Buddhist scriptures. The court granted the canon along with the emperor's own works Secret Canon Exegesis, Roaming Chants, and Lotus Heart Wheel.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，治遣使白思柔貢方物並謝賜經及御制。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Zhi sent the envoy Bai Sirou with local products and to thank them for the granted scriptures and imperial compositions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year (993), Zhi sent Bai Sirou with regional goods to thank the court for the canon and imperial writings.

sentences.zh: 二月，遣秘書丞直史館陳靖、秘書丞劉式爲使，加治檢校太師，仍降詔存問軍吏耆老。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Secretariat Assistant Director on duty at the Historiography Institute Chen Jing and Secretariat Assistant Director Liu Shi were sent as envoys; Zhi was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor, and an edict was also issued to inquire after military officers and elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Chen Jing, Secretariat Assistant Director on duty at the Historiography Institute, and Liu Shi, Secretariat Assistant Director, were dispatched as envoys. Zhi was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor, and an edict was issued to inquire after his officers and elders.

sentences.zh: 靖等自東牟趣八角海口，得思柔所乘海船及高麗水工，即登舟自芝岡島順風泛大海，再宿抵甕津口登陸，行百六十里抵高麗之境曰海州，又百里至閻州，又四十里至白州，又四十里至其國。

translations.literal: Jing and the others set out from Dongmou toward Bajiao Sea Harbor, obtained the seagoing ship Sirou had used and Goryeo sailors, then boarded and from Zhigang Island sailed with the wind across the great sea; after two nights they reached Wengjin Harbor and went ashore, traveled one hundred sixty li to the Goryeo border district called Haizhou, another hundred li to Yanzhou, another forty li to Baizhou, and another forty li to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's party left Dongmou for Bajiao Harbor, took Sirou's ship and Goryeo sailors, and from Zhigang Island sailed with a fair wind across the open sea. After two nights they landed at Wengjin Harbor, traveled one hundred sixty li to the Goryeo border district of Haizhou, then a hundred li to Yanzhou, forty li to Baizhou, and forty li more to the capital.

sentences.zh: 治迎使於郊，盡藩臣禮，延留靖等七十餘日而還，遺以襲衣、金帶、金銀器數百兩、布三萬餘端，附表稱謝。

translations.literal: Zhi welcomed the envoys in the suburbs with full feudal-subject ceremony, detained Jing and the others more than seventy days before their return, and gave them ceremonial robes, gold belts, several hundred taels of gold and silver vessels, and more than thirty thousand bolts of cloth, attaching a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi welcomed them in the suburbs with full ceremony befitting a feudatory, kept them more than seventy days, then sent them home with ceremonial robes, gold belts, several hundred taels of gold and silver vessels, and more than thirty thousand bolts of cloth, together with a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 先是，三年，上親試諸道貢舉人，詔賜高麗賓貢進士王彬、崔罕等及第，既授以官，遣還本國。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the third year, the emperor personally examined tribute candidates from all circuits; an edict granted the Goryeo guest-tribute jinshi Wang Bin, Cui Han, and others passage in the examination; after offices were conferred they were sent back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the third year (992), the emperor personally examined tribute candidates from all circuits and granted the Goryeo students Wang Bin and Cui Han passage in the jinshi examination. After appointing them to office, the court sent them home.

sentences.zh: 至是，靖等使回，治上表謝曰：「學生王彬、崔罕等入朝習業，蒙恩並賜及第，授將仕郎、守秘書省校書郎，仍放歸本國。

translations.literal: At this time, when Jing and the others returned, Zhi submitted a memorial of thanks, saying: 'The students Wang Bin, Cui Han, and others came to court to pursue studies, received grace and were both granted examination success, appointed Junior Gentleman and Acting Collator of the Secretariat, and still released to return to their native country.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing returned, Zhi submitted a memorial of thanks: 'Our students Wang Bin and Cui Han came to court to study. Your Majesty graciously granted them the jinshi degree and appointed them Junior Gentleman and Acting Collator of the Secretariat, then allowed them to return home.

sentences.zh: 竊以當道薦修貢奉，多曆歲年，蓋以上國天高，遐荒海隔，不獲躬趨金闕，面叩玉階，唯深拱極之誠，莫展來庭之禮。

translations.literal: We venture that our authorities have long presented tribute through many years; because the upper state's heaven is high and the distant wilds are separated by sea, we could not personally hasten to the golden palace or face the jade steps—only deep sincerity of bowing toward the pole, without being able to display the ceremony of coming to court.
translations.idiomatic: Our realm has sent tribute for many years, but the Son of Heaven sits high above and our distant land lies across the sea. We cannot ourselves hurry to the golden palace or kneel before the jade steps—we can only bow toward the throne in spirit, never perform the rite of attending court in person.

sentences.zh: 彬、罕等幼從匏系，嗟混跡於嵎夷；

translations.literal: Bin, Han, and the others from youth followed the gourd tether, sighing that they mingled their traces in the eastern wilds;
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Han, bound from youth to our distant realm, had long resigned themselves to life at the edge of the world;

sentences.zh: 不憚蓬飄，早賓王於天邑。

translations.literal: not fearing tumbleweed drifting, they early became guests of the king in the heavenly capital.
translations.idiomatic: yet without fearing the wanderer's hardships they came early as guests to the celestial capital.

sentences.zh: 縕袍短褐，玉粒桂薪，堪憂食貧，若爲卒歲。

translations.literal: Worn robes and short hempen coats, jade grain and cassia firewood—they could worry over poverty of food, as if how to finish the year.
translations.idiomatic: In worn robes and coarse clothes, with plain grain and firewood for fuel, they lived in poverty and wondered how they would survive the year.

sentences.zh: 皇帝陛下天慈照毓，海量優容，豐其館穀之資，勖以藝文之業。

translations.literal: Your Majesty the Emperor, heaven's kindness shining on and nurturing them, sea-like magnanimity graciously tolerating, enriched their lodging and grain supplies, and exhorted them in literary arts.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heavenly kindness nourished them, your ocean-like forbearance embraced them, you enriched their lodging and provisions, and encouraged their literary studies.

sentences.zh: 去歲高懸軒鑒，大選魯儒，彬、罕接武澤宮，敢萌心於中鵠；

translations.literal: Last year the lofty mirror was hung high and the great selection of Lu scholars was held; Bin and Han followed in the marsh palace succession, daring to conceive in their hearts hitting the target center;
translations.idiomatic: Last year Your Majesty held the great examination. Bin and Han entered the competition alongside the scholars of the capital and dared hope to hit the mark;

sentences.zh: 濫巾英域，空有志於羨魚。

translations.literal: they indiscriminately joined the cap in the splendid realm, vainly having ambition like envying fish.
translations.idiomatic: they took their place among the empire's finest scholars, though they scarcely dared hope for success.

sentences.zh: 陛下以其萬里辭家，十年觀國，俾登名于桂籍，仍命秩於芸台；

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because they left home ten thousand li and observed the state for ten years, caused their names to be entered on the cassia register and still assigned rank at the Book Repository;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, seeing that they had left home ten thousand li and studied in the capital for ten years, placed their names on the jinshi rolls and appointed them to the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 憫其懷土之心，慰以倚門之望，別垂宸旨，令歸故鄉。

translations.literal: pitied their hearts longing for home, comforted the hope of those leaning on the gate, and specially bestowed an imperial intent ordering them to return to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: pitied their longing for home and the parents waiting at their gates, and specially decreed that they return to their homeland.

sentences.zh: 玄造曲成，鴻恩莫報，臣不勝感天戴聖之至。」

translations.literal: The dark creator completed them with favor; the great grace cannot be repaid—your subject is overcome with feeling heaven and bearing the sage to the utmost.'
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's design has favored us beyond measure; such grace cannot be repaid. Your servant is overcome with gratitude to Heaven and to Your sacred person.'

sentences.zh: 又有張仁銓者，進奉使白思柔之孔目吏也，上書獻便宜。

translations.literal: There was also Zhang Renquan, a clerical officer of the tribute envoy Bai Sirou, who submitted a memorial offering timely proposals.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhang Renquan, a clerical officer attached to the tribute envoy Bai Sirou, who submitted a memorial with policy recommendations.

sentences.zh: 思柔意其持國陰事以告，仁銓懼不敢歸。

translations.literal: Sirou suspected he was reporting the country's secret affairs, and Renquan, afraid, did not dare return.
translations.idiomatic: Sirou suspected he had disclosed state secrets, and Renquan, fearing punishment, dared not return home.

sentences.zh: 上命靖等領以還國，仍詔治釋仁銓罪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jing and the others to lead him back to his country, and also edicted Zhi to release Renquan from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jing to escort him home and edicted Zhi to pardon Renquan.

sentences.zh: 治又上表謝曰：「官告國信使陳靖、劉式至，奉傳聖旨，以當道進奉使從行孔目官張仁銓至闕，輒進便宜，翻懷憂懼，今附使臣帶歸本國者。

translations.literal: Zhi again submitted a memorial of thanks, saying: 'The credential-bearing envoys Chen Jing and Liu Shi have arrived, conveying the sage decree that Zhang Renquan, the clerical officer accompanying our tribute envoy, came to the palace and rashly submitted timely proposals, instead harboring worry and fear—now he is attached to the envoy to be brought back to our country.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi submitted another memorial of thanks: 'Imperial envoys Chen Jing and Liu Shi have arrived bearing Your decree regarding Zhang Renquan, the clerk who accompanied our tribute mission. He came to court and submitted recommendations, then feared reprisal. He is now returning with your envoys to our country.

sentences.zh: 仁銓嵎宅細民，海門賤吏，獲趨上國，敢貢愚誠，罔思狂瞽之尤，輒奏權宜之事，妄塵旒冕，上黷朝廷。

translations.literal: Renquan was a hermit-household petty commoner, a humble official of Haimen; having gained access to the superior state, he dared offer his foolish sincerity, heedless of the fault of reckless blindness, and rashly memorialized expedient matters, presumptuously defiling the imperial canopy and offending the court above.
translations.idiomatic: Renquan was a commoner of secluded household status and a lowly officer at Haimen. Gaining access to the imperial court, he dared offer his humble counsel without reflecting on the recklessness of his presumption, rashly submitting policy proposals that defiled Your Majesty's presence and offended the court.

sentences.zh: 今者，仰奉綸言，釋其罪罟。

translations.literal: Now, looking up to receive your corded words, his net of guilt is released.
translations.idiomatic: Now, receiving Your gracious edict from above, his bonds of guilt are loosed.

sentences.zh: 小人趨利，豈虞僭越之求，聖主寬恩，遠降哀矜之命。

translations.literal: A petty man seeks profit—how could he have anticipated a request to overstep? The sage ruler's generous grace reaches far, bestowing a command of pity and sparing.
translations.idiomatic: A petty man chases gain—who could have foreseen his overreaching? Yet the sage ruler's mercy reaches from afar, bestowing a command of compassion and pardon.

sentences.zh: 其張仁銓者已依詔旨放罪，令掌事如故。」

translations.literal: As for Zhang Renquan, he has already been released from guilt according to the edict, and ordered to manage affairs as before.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Renquan has been pardoned according to the edict and restored to his former duties.'

sentences.zh: 又上言願賜板本《九經》書，用敦儒教，許之。

translations.literal: Closing the memorial, he also submitted a petition requesting block-printed copies of the Nine Classics to promote Confucian teaching; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned for block-printed copies of the Nine Classics to advance Confucian learning; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 先是，式等復命，治遣使元證衍送之，證衍至安香浦口，值風損船，溺所齎物。

translations.literal: Previously, when Shi and the others reported back, Zhi sent the envoy Yuan Zhengyan to escort them. Zhengyan reached Anxiang harbor mouth, encountered wind that damaged the ship, and the goods he carried were sunk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Shi and the others returned to report, Zhi sent the envoy Yuan Zhengyan to escort them home. Zhengyan reached Anxiang Harbor, where a storm damaged the ship and everything he carried was lost at sea.

sentences.zh: 詔登州給證衍文據遣還，仍賜治衣段二百匹、銀器二百兩、羊五十口。

translations.literal: The court edicted Deng Prefecture to provide Zhengyan with travel documents to send him back, and also bestowed on Zhi two hundred bolts of cloth, two hundred taels of silver vessels, and fifty sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Deng Prefecture to issue Zhengyan travel documents for his return and additionally bestowed on Zhi two hundred bolts of silk, two hundred taels of silverware, and fifty sheep.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，遣使元郁來乞師，訴以契丹寇境。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, he sent the envoy Yuan Yu to beg for troops, complaining that the Khitan were raiding the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year, he sent the envoy Yuan Yu to request military aid, reporting that the Khitan were invading his borders.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以北鄙甫寧，不可輕動干戈，爲國生事，但賜詔慰撫，厚禮其使遣還。

translations.literal: The court considered that the northern frontier had only just been pacified and arms must not be lightly stirred to create troubles for the state; they merely bestowed an edict of consolation, treated the envoy generously, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged that the northern frontier had only just settled and that arms must not be lightly moved to stir trouble for the realm. They issued only a consoling edict, treated the envoy with generous gifts, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 自是受制於契丹，朝貢中絕。

translations.literal: From this time Goryeo was subject to the Khitan and tribute missions to China ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From this point Goryeo fell under Khitan control, and tribute missions to the Song ceased.

sentences.zh: 治卒，弟誦立。

translations.literal: Zhi died; his younger brother Song succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi died, and his younger brother Song succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣兵校徐遠來候朝廷德音，遠久不至。

translations.literal: He once sent the military officer Xu Yuan to await the court's gracious pronouncement, but Yuan was long in not arriving.
translations.idiomatic: He once dispatched the military officer Xu Yuan to await the court's gracious edict, but Yuan was long delayed and never arrived.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，其臣吏部侍郎趙之遴命牙將朱仁紹至登州偵之，州將以聞，上特召見仁紹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, his minister, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Zhao Zhili, ordered the junior officer Zhu Renshao to Deng Prefecture to spy things out; the prefect reported this, and the emperor specially summoned Renshao for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping (1000), his minister Zhao Zhili, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, sent the junior officer Zhu Renshao to Deng Prefecture to reconnoiter. The prefect reported this, and the emperor personally summoned Renshao for an audience.

sentences.zh: 因自陳國人思慕皇化，爲契丹羈制之狀，乃賜誦函詔一道，令仁紹齎還。

translations.literal: He thereupon stated of his own accord that the people of the country yearned for imperial civilization and described how they were restrained by the Khitan; the emperor then bestowed Song one sealed edict and ordered Renshao to carry it back.
translations.idiomatic: Renshao then described how the people yearned for the Song's civilizing influence and how they were constrained by the Khitan. The emperor bestowed on Song a sealed edict and ordered Renshao to carry it home.

sentences.zh: 六年，誦遣使戶部郎中李宣古來朝謝恩，且言：「晉割燕薊以屬契丹，遂有路趣玄菟，屢來攻伐，求取不已，乞王師屯境上爲之牽制。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Song sent the envoy Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Li Xuanggu to court to thank for imperial grace, and moreover said: 'When Jin ceded Yan and Ji to belong to the Khitan, a route then led toward Xuantu; they have repeatedly come attacking, ceaselessly seeking to seize; we beg that Your army camp on the borders to restrain them.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Song sent the envoy Li Xuanggu, Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, to court to express gratitude, reporting: 'When the Jin ceded Yan and Ji to the Khitan, a route opened toward Xuantu. They have attacked again and again, demanding more without end. We beg that Your armies camp on the border to hold them in check.'

sentences.zh: 詔書優答之。

translations.literal: Closing the memorial, an edict graciously replied.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued a gracious written reply.

sentences.zh: 誦卒，弟詢權知國事。

translations.literal: Song died; his younger brother Xun provisionally managed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Song died, and his younger brother Xun assumed provisional control of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹既襲高麗，遂築六城曰興州、曰鐵州、曰通州、曰龍州、曰龜州、曰郭州於境上。

translations.literal: Previously, after the Khitan had raided Goryeo, they then built six cities on the border called Xing Prefecture, Tie Prefecture, Tong Prefecture, Long Prefecture, Gui Prefecture, and Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the Khitan had attacked Goryeo, they built six fortified cities on the border: Xing, Tie, Tong, Long, Gui, and Guo.

sentences.zh: 契丹以爲貳己，遣使來求六城，詢不許。

translations.literal: The Khitan, taking this as disloyalty to themselves, sent envoys to demand the six cities; Xun did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan regarded this as disloyalty and sent envoys to demand the six cities. Xun refused.

sentences.zh: 遂舉兵，奄至城下，焚蕩宮室，剽劫居人，詢徙居升羅州以避之。

translations.literal: They thereupon raised troops, suddenly arriving below the walls, burning and sweeping the palaces, plundering the inhabitants; Xun moved his residence to Shengluo Prefecture to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then raised an army that swept to the walls, burned the palaces, and plundered the populace. Xun relocated to Shengluo Prefecture to escape them.

sentences.zh: 兵退，乃遣使請和。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew, he then sent envoys to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, he sent envoys to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 契丹堅以六城爲辭，自是調兵守六城。

translations.literal: The Khitan insisted on the six cities as their plea; from this time they deployed troops to garrison the six cities.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan insisted on the six cities as the price of peace and thereafter stationed troops to hold them.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，大舉來伐，詢與女真設奇邀擊，殺契丹殆盡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, they mounted a major campaign to attack; Xun, with the Jurchen, set an ambuscade to intercept them and slaughtered the Khitan nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1010), the Khitan launched a major invasion. Xun allied with the Jurchen to ambush them and killed nearly the entire Khitan force.

sentences.zh: 詢又於鴨綠江東築城，與來遠城相望，跨江爲橋，潛兵以固新城。

translations.literal: Xun also built a city east of the Yalu River, facing Laiyuan City across the river, spanning the river with a bridge, and stationed troops in secret to secure the new city.
translations.idiomatic: Xun also built a city east of the Yalu River opposite Laiyuan, spanning the river with a bridge and stationing troops in secret to fortify the new city.

sentences.zh: 七年，方遣告奏使御事工部侍郎尹證古以金線織成龍鳳鞍並繡龍鳳鞍襆各二幅、細馬二匹、散馬二十匹來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, just as he was sending the memorial envoy Vice Director of Works under the Sovereign's Service Yin Zhenggu, bearing two gold-thread-woven dragon-phoenix saddles and two embroidered dragon-phoenix saddle cushions each, two fine horses, and twenty ordinary horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, he was sending the memorial envoy Yin Zhenggu, Vice Director of Works under the Sovereign's Service, bearing two gold-thread-woven dragon-phoenix saddles, two embroidered dragon-phoenix saddle cushions, two fine horses, and twenty ordinary horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 證古還，賜詢詔書七通並衣帶、銀彩、鞍勒馬等。

translations.literal: When Zhenggu returned, Xun was granted seven edicts together with robes, belts, silver brocade, saddled horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenggu returned, Xun received seven imperial edicts along with robes, belts, silver brocade, saddled horses, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔登州置館於海次以待使者。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered Deng Prefecture to establish a lodge by the sea to await envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the court ordered Deng Prefecture to establish a guest lodge on the coast to receive envoys.

sentences.zh: 其年，又遣御事民官侍郎郭元來貢。

translations.literal: That year, he again sent the Vice Director of Civil Affairs under the Sovereign's Service Guo Yuan as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he again sent Guo Yuan, Vice Director of Civil Affairs under the Sovereign's Service, with tribute.

sentences.zh: 元自言：「本國城無垣牆，府曰開城，管六縣，民不下三五千。

translations.literal: Yuan said of his own accord: 'Our country's capital has no enclosing walls; the prefectural seat is called Kaesong, governing six counties, with fewer than three to five thousand inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan reported: 'Our capital has no city walls. The seat of government is called Kaesong, administering six counties with no more than three to five thousand inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 有州軍百餘，置十路轉運司統之。

translations.literal: There are more than a hundred prefectures and garrisons, managed under ten circuit transport commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has more than a hundred prefectures and military districts, governed by ten circuit transport commissioners.

sentences.zh: 每州管縣五六，小者亦三四，每縣戶三四百。

translations.literal: Each prefecture governs five or six counties, smaller ones three or four; each county has three to four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture administers five or six counties—smaller ones three or four—with three to four hundred households per county.

sentences.zh: 國境南北千五百里，東西二千里。

translations.literal: The realm from north to south is fifteen hundred li, east to west two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The realm measures fifteen hundred li north to south and two thousand li east to west.

sentences.zh: 軍民雜處，隸軍者不黥面。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians live mingled; those enrolled in the army are not tattooed on the face.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians live intermingled. Those enrolled in the army are not tattooed on the face.

sentences.zh: 方午爲市，不用錢，第以布米貿易。

translations.literal: At midday they hold markets; they do not use coin, but trade only in cloth and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Markets open at noon. They use no currency, trading only in cloth and grain.

sentences.zh: 地宜粳稻，風俗頗類中國。

translations.literal: The land suits japonica rice; customs resemble China rather closely.
translations.idiomatic: The land is suited to japonica rice, and customs closely resemble those of China.

sentences.zh: 無羊、兔、橐駝、水牛、驢。

translations.literal: There are no sheep, rabbits, camels, water buffalo, or donkeys.
translations.idiomatic: There are no sheep, rabbits, camels, water buffalo, or donkeys.

sentences.zh: 氣候少寒，暑差多。

translations.literal: The climate has little cold; there is rather more heat.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is mild, with little cold and rather more heat.

sentences.zh: 有僧，無道士。

translations.literal: There are Buddhist monks; there are no Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: There are Buddhist monks but no Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 民家器皿，悉銅爲之。

translations.literal: Household utensils are all made of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Household utensils are all made of copper.

sentences.zh: 樂有二品：曰唐樂，曰鄉樂。

translations.literal: Music has two kinds: called Tang music and native music.
translations.idiomatic: Music falls into two categories: Tang music and native music.

sentences.zh: 三歲一試舉人，有進士、諸科、算學，每試百餘人，登第者不過一二十。

translations.literal: Every three years they test scholars; there are jinshi, various examination categories, and mathematical study; each examination has more than a hundred candidates, but those who pass number no more than ten or twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years the civil examinations are held, with jinshi, specialized categories, and mathematical study. Each session draws more than a hundred candidates, but no more than ten or twenty pass.

sentences.zh: 每正月一日、五月五日祭祖禰廟。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month and the fifth day of the fifth month they sacrifice at the ancestral temple of father and grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month and the fifth day of the fifth month they sacrifice at the ancestral temple to father and grandfather.

sentences.zh: 又正月七日，家爲王母像戴之。

translations.literal: Again, on the seventh day of the first month, each household makes an image of the Queen Mother and wears it.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the first month, each household fashions an image of the Queen Mother and wears it.

sentences.zh: 二月望，僧俗燃燈如中國上元節。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth of the second month, monks and laity light lamps as in China's Lantern Festival.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the second month, monks and laypeople light lamps as in China's Lantern Festival.

sentences.zh: 上巳日，以青艾染餅爲盤羞之冠。

translations.literal: On the Shangsi day, they dye cakes with green mugwort to crown the tray of delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: On the Shangsi festival, they dye cakes with green mugwort to crown the ceremonial food tray.

sentences.zh: 端午有秋千之戲。

translations.literal: At the Dragon Boat Festival there is the swing game.
translations.idiomatic: At the Dragon Boat Festival they play on swings.

sentences.zh: 士女服尚素。

translations.literal: Men and women favor plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women favor plain, undyed clothing.

sentences.zh: 地產龍須席、藤席、白︴紙、鼠狼尾筆。」

translations.literal: Local products include dragon-whisker mats, rattan mats, mulberry paper, and sable-tail brushes.'
translations.idiomatic: Local products include dragon-whisker mats, rattan mats, mulberry paper, and sable-tail brushes.'

sentences.zh: 元辭貌恭恪，每受宴賜，必自爲謝表，粗有文采，朝廷待之亦厚。

translations.literal: Closing his account, Yuan was respectful and deferential in bearing; whenever he received a banquet gift, he always composed his own thanks memorial, with some literary polish; the court also treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan was respectful and deferential in manner. Whenever he received a banquet gift, he composed his own thank-you memorial, showing modest literary skill. The court treated him generously as well.

sentences.zh: 九年，辭還，賜詢詔書七函，襲衣、金帶、器幣、鞍馬及經史、曆日、《聖惠方》等。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on taking leave to return, Xun was granted seven caskets of edicts, investiture robes, gold belt, ritual vessels, saddled horses, and the Classics and histories, calendars, Imperial Grace Formulary, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, on his departure, Xun received seven caskets of edicts, investiture robes, a gold belt, ritual vessels, saddled horses, the Classics and histories, calendars, the Imperial Grace Formulary, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 元又請錄《國朝登科記》及所賜御詩以歸，從之。

translations.literal: Yuan also requested copies of Records of Jinshi Graduates of Our Dynasty and the imperial poems bestowed on him to take home; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan also requested copies of the Records of Jinshi Graduates of Our Dynasty and the imperial poems he had received, to carry home. His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，遣御事刑官侍郎徐訥奉表獻方物於崇政殿，又賀封建壽春郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, he sent the Vice Director of Penal Affairs under the Sovereign's Service Xu Ne to present a memorial and tribute goods at Chongzheng Hall, and also to congratulate on the enfeoffment of the Prince of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi (1017), he sent Xu Ne, Vice Director of Penal Affairs under the Sovereign's Service, to present a memorial and tribute at Chongzheng Hall and to congratulate the enfeoffment of the Prince of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，登州言高麗進奉使禮賓卿崔元信至秦王水口，遭風覆舟，漂失貢物，詔遣內臣撫之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, Deng Prefecture reported that the Goryeo tribute envoy Director of Ceremonies Cui Yuanxin reached the Prince of Qin Water Mouth, encountered wind that capsized the boat, and drifted away the tribute goods; an edict dispatched an inner attendant to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year, Deng Prefecture reported that the Goryeo tribute envoy Cui Yuanxin, Director of Ceremonies, had reached Qinwangshui Harbor when a storm capsized his boat and the tribute goods were lost. The court dispatched an inner attendant to console them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，元信等入見，貢罽錦衣褥、烏漆甲、金飾長刀匕首、罽錦鞍馬、紵布藥物等，又進中布二千端，求佛經一藏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yuanxin and the others entered audience, presenting felt brocade robes and coverlets, black lacquer armor, gold-decorated long knives and daggers, felt brocade saddled horses, ramie cloth medicines, and the like; they also presented two thousand bolts of medium cloth and requested one complete canon of Buddhist sutras.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Yuanxin and his party were received in audience, presenting felt brocade robes and coverlets, black lacquer armor, gold-decorated long knives and daggers, felt brocade saddled horses, ramie cloth, medicines, and other goods. They also offered two thousand bolts of medium-grade cloth and requested a complete Buddhist canon.

sentences.zh: 詔賜經還布，以元信覆溺匱乏，別賜衣服、繒彩焉。

translations.literal: An edict granted the sutras and returned the cloth; because Yuanxin had been capsized and was destitute, they separately bestowed robes and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the sutras and returned the cloth. Because Yuanxin had been shipwrecked and was destitute, additional robes and silks were bestowed separately.

sentences.zh: 明州、登州屢言高麗海船有風漂至境上者，詔令存問，給度海糧遣還，仍爲著例。

translations.literal: Ming and Deng prefectures repeatedly reported that Goryeo sea ships had been blown by wind to drift within the borders; an edict ordered them to inquire after their welfare, provide grain for crossing the sea, and send them back, and this was made a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ming and Deng prefectures repeatedly reported Goryeo ships blown by storms into Song waters. The court ordered officials to inquire after their welfare, provide provisions for the sea crossing, and send them home—establishing this as a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 五年，詢遣告奏使御事禮部侍郎韓祚等一百七十九人來謝恩，且言與契丹修好，又表乞陰陽地理書、《聖惠方》，並賜之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Xun sent the memorial envoy Vice Director of Rites under the Sovereign's Service Han Zuo and 179 others to thank for grace, and moreover reported that they had made peace with the Khitan; they also memorialized begging for books on yin-yang and geography and the Imperial Grace Formulary; all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Xun sent the memorial envoy Han Zuo, Vice Director of Rites under the Sovereign's Service, with 179 others to express gratitude and report that peace had been made with the Khitan. They also requested books on yin-yang and geography and the Imperial Grace Formulary—all of which were granted.

sentences.zh: 金行成者，累官至殿中丞，治表乞放還。

translations.literal: Kim Haengseong had risen through many offices to Defender of the Hall; Zhi memorialized begging to release him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Kim Haengseong had risen through many offices to Defender of the Hall. Zhi memorialized requesting permission for him to return home.

sentences.zh: 行成自以筮仕朝廷，不願歸本國。

translations.literal: Haengseong himself, having taken office in the Song court by divination appointment, did not wish to return to his native country.
translations.idiomatic: Haengseong himself, having entered Song service through the tribute-scholar path, did not wish to return to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 又以父母垂老，在海外旦暮思念，恨祿不及，令工圖其像置正寢，與妻史氏居旁室，晨夕定省上食，未嘗少懈。

translations.literal: Moreover, because his parents were advanced in years overseas, morning and evening he longed for them; regretting that his salary could not reach them, he had artisans paint their portraits and place them in the main chamber; he and his wife Lady Shi dwelt in a side room, morning and evening performing obeisance and offering food, never slackening in the least.
translations.idiomatic: His parents were elderly in Goryeo, and he longed for them morning and night, grieving that his salary could not reach them. He had artisans paint their portraits and placed them in the main chamber. He and his wife Lady Shi lived in a side room, performing obeisance and offering food morning and evening without ever slackening.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，通判安州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, he served as Vice Administrative Commissioner of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chunhua era, he served as vice administrative commissioner of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 被病，知州李範與僚佐數人省之，行成病已篤，泣且言曰：「行成外國人，爲朝官，佐郡政，病且死，未有以報主恩，雖瞑目固有遺恨。

translations.literal: He fell ill; Prefect Li Fan and several staff members visited him. Haengseong's illness was already grave; weeping he said: 'Haengseong is a foreigner who became a court official and assisted in prefectural governance; sick and about to die, I have no means to repay the ruler's grace—though I close my eyes, regret surely remains.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill. Prefect Li Fan and several staff members visited him. Haengseong was gravely ill and wept as he spoke: 'I am a foreigner who became a court official and assisted in governing this prefecture. Sick and dying, I have no way to repay the ruler's grace. Even in death, regret will remain.

sentences.zh: 二子宗敏、宗訥皆幼，家素貧，無他親可依，旦暮委溝壑矣。」

translations.literal: My two sons Zongmin and Zongne are both young; the family has always been poor with no other kin to rely on; morning and evening they will be cast into ditches and gullies.'
translations.idiomatic: My two sons Zongmin and Zongne are still young. Our family has always been poor, with no other kin to rely on. Soon they will be cast into ditches and gullies.'

sentences.zh: 未幾，行成死，其妻養二子，誓不嫁，織履以給。

translations.literal: Before long Haengseong died; his wife raised the two sons, vowed not to remarry, and wove shoes to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Haengseong died. His wife raised the two sons, vowed never to remarry, and wove shoes to support them.

sentences.zh: 範表其事，詔以宗敏補太廟齋郎，令安州月給其家錢三緡、米五斛，長吏歲時存問。

translations.literal: Fan memorialized the matter; an edict appointed Zongmin as Junior Attendant at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, ordered An Prefecture to grant the family three strings of cash and five piculs of grain monthly, and the chief official to visit them at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan memorialized the matter. The court appointed Zongmin as Junior Attendant at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, ordered An Prefecture to grant the family three strings of cash and five piculs of grain each month, and directed the prefect to visit them at the seasons.

sentences.zh: 又高麗信州永甯人康戩，字休祐，父允，三世爲兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: There was also Kang Jian of Yongning in Sin Prefecture, Goryeo, style name Xiuyou; his father Yun—three generations had served as Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Kang Jian of Yongning in Sin Prefecture, Goryeo, courtesy name Xiuyou. His father Yun had served as Vice Director of the Ministry of War for three generations.

sentences.zh: 戩少好學，時紇升與契丹交兵，戩從允戰木葉山下，連中二矢，神色不變。

translations.literal: Jian in youth loved learning; when Goryeo and the Khitan were at war, Jian followed Yun in battle below Muyeok Mountain, struck twice by arrows, his expression unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jian loved learning from youth. When Goryeo and the Khitan were at war, he followed Yun into battle below Muyeok Mountain and was struck twice by arrows without changing expression.

sentences.zh: 後陷契丹，遁居墨斗嶺，又至黃龍府，間道得歸高麗，時允猶在。

translations.literal: Later captured by the Khitan, he fled and dwelt on Ink Dipper Ridge, then reached Huanglong Prefecture, and by secret route returned to Goryeo; Yun was still alive at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Later captured by the Khitan, he escaped to Ink Dipper Ridge, then reached Huanglong Prefecture, and by a secret route made his way back to Goryeo while Yun was still alive.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，允遣戩隨賓貢肄業國學。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao period, Yun sent Jian to follow the tribute scholars to study at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era, Yun sent Jian to accompany the tribute scholars to study at the National University.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，登進士第，解褐大理評事，知湘鄉縣，再遷著作佐朗，知江陰軍、江州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination, took off the mourning garments as Assistant Making Judgments at Court of Judicial Review, governed Xiangxiang County; promoted again to Assistant Author at the Palace Library, governed Jiangyin Military Prefecture and Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo (980) he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Assistant Making Judgments at the Court of Judicial Review, and governed Xiangxiang County. He was later promoted to Assistant Author at the Palace Library and governed Jiangyin Military Prefecture and Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曆官以清白乾力聞，改太常博士。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he was known for integrity and efficiency; changed to Erudite at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive offices he was known for integrity and capability and was appointed Erudite at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 蘇易簡在翰林，稱其吏才，命爲廣南西路轉運副使，賜緋魚，就遷正使，再轉度支員外郎、戶部判官。

translations.literal: Su Yijian was at the Hanlin Academy and praised his administrative talent; he was appointed Vice Transport Commissioner of the Guangnan West Circuit, granted scarlet fish tokens; promoted in place to chief commissioner; then transferred to Vice Director of Revenue in the outer office, Bureau of Revenue Judge.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian at the Hanlin Academy praised his administrative talent and had him appointed Vice Transport Commissioner of the Guangnan West Circuit with scarlet fish tokens. He was promoted in place to chief commissioner, then to Vice Director of Revenue in the outer office and Bureau of Revenue Judge.

sentences.zh: 出知峽、越二州，連被詔褒其能政。

translations.literal: Sent out to govern Xia and Yue prefectures; repeatedly received edicts praising his capable governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Xia and Yue prefectures and repeatedly received imperial edicts praising his capable administration.

sentences.zh: 又爲京西轉運使，加工部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Again made Transport Commissioner of the Jingxi Circuit, added Ministry of Works Director, granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Transport Commissioner of the Jingxi Circuit, promoted to Ministry of Works Director, and granted gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 戩所至好行事，上章多建白，以竭誠自任。

translations.literal: Wherever Jian went he was fond of taking action; memorials to the throne were many with constructive proposals, taking full dedication as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Jian served he was eager to act. His memorials to the throne were full of constructive proposals, and he took complete dedication as his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，卒，真宗特以其子希齡爲太常寺奉禮郎，給奉終喪。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde he died; Emperor Zhenzong specially appointed his son Xiling as Junior Master of Ceremonies at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granting salary through the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingde (1006) he died. Emperor Zhenzong specially appointed his son Xiling as Junior Master of Ceremonies at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with salary granted through the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年二月，祚等辭歸國，賜詢如故事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianxing, Zuo and the others took leave to return home; Xun was granted gifts according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Qianxing (1022), Han Zuo and his party took leave to return home. Xun received gifts according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 會真宗晏駕，又齎遺物以賜詢。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhenzong passed away; they also carried heirloom objects to bestow on Xun.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Emperor Zhenzong had passed away, and they also carried heirlooms from the late emperor to bestow on Xun.

sentences.zh: 天聖八年，詢復遣御事民官侍郎元穎等二百九十三人奉表入見於長春殿，貢金器、銀罽刀劍、鞍勒馬、香油、人參、細布、銅器、硫黃、青鼠皮等物。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiansheng, Xun again sent the Vice Director of Civil Affairs under the Sovereign's Service Yuan Ying and 293 others to present a memorial and enter audience at Changchun Hall, offering gold vessels, silver felt knives and swords, saddled horses, sesame oil, ginseng, fine cloth, copper vessels, sulfur, sable pelts, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tiansheng (1030), Xun again sent Yuan Ying, Vice Director of Civil Affairs under the Sovereign's Service, with 293 others to present a memorial and enter audience at Changchun Hall, offering gold vessels, silver felt, knives, swords, saddled horses, sesame oil, ginseng, fine cloth, copper vessels, sulfur, sable pelts, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 明年二月辭歸，賜予有差，遣使護送至登州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year on taking leave to return, grants were differentiated; envoys were dispatched to escort them to Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year they took leave to return. Gifts were granted according to rank, and envoys were dispatched to escort them to Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其後絕不通中國者四十三年。

translations.literal: After this, communications with China ceased for forty-three years.
translations.idiomatic: After this, contact with China ceased for forty-three years.

sentences.zh: 詢孫徽嗣立，是爲文王。

translations.literal: Xun's grandson Hui succeeded and was known as King Mun.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's grandson Hui succeeded him and is known as King Mun.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，其國禮賓省移牒福建轉運使羅拯云：「本朝商人黃真、洪萬來稱，運使奉密旨，令招接通好。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, the country's Directorate of Ceremonies sent a dispatch to Fujian Transport Commissioner Luo Cheng, stating: 'Merchants of our court Huang Zhen and Hong Wan came saying that the transport commissioner received a secret decree ordering them to summon and restore friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xining (1069), Goryeo's Directorate of Ceremonies sent a dispatch to Fujian Transport Commissioner Luo Cheng stating: 'Our merchants Huang Zhen and Hong Wan report that the transport commissioner received a secret decree ordering them to restore friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 奉國王旨意，形於部述。

translations.literal: In accord with the king's command, this is set forth in a departmental memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In accordance with the king's command, this is set forth in our memorial.

sentences.zh: 當國僻居暘谷，邈戀天朝，頃從祖禰以來，素願梯航相繼。

translations.literal: Our state dwells remote in the Valley of the Rising Sun, yet longs distantly for the Celestial Court; for generations since our forefathers we have always wished that ladder-and-raft embassies continue in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Our state lies remote in the eastern sunlands, yet yearns for the Celestial Court. Since our forefathers' time we have always wished that embassies by sea might continue in succession.

sentences.zh: 蕞爾平壤，邇於大遼，附之則爲睦鄰，疏之則爲勍敵。

translations.literal: Tiny Pyongyang lies near Great Liao; draw near and we have a friendly neighbor; keep distant and we have a formidable foe.
translations.idiomatic: Our small realm of Pyongyang lies close to Great Liao. Draw near and we have a friendly neighbor; keep distant and we face a formidable enemy.

sentences.zh: 慮邊騷之弗息，蓄陸詟以靡遑。

translations.literal: Fearing that border troubles would not cease, we amassed awe on land until we had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing unceasing border troubles, we amassed forces on land until we had no leisure for anything else.

sentences.zh: 久困羈縻，難圖攜貳，故違述職，致有積年。

translations.literal: Long constrained in tributary bonds, hard to contemplate dual allegiance; therefore we neglected our duty of reporting and years have piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Long constrained by tributary obligations to Liao, we could not contemplate divided loyalties. Thus we neglected our reporting duties, and the years have accumulated.

sentences.zh: 屢卜雲祥，雖美聖辰於中國；

translations.literal: Repeatedly we divined auspicious clouds—though they blessed the sacred reign in China;
translations.idiomatic: Again and again we read auspicious omens in the clouds—omens that blessed the sacred reign in China;

sentences.zh: 空知日遠，如迷舊路于長安。

translations.literal: in vain we knew the sun was far, as if lost on the old road to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: yet in vain we knew the sun was far away, as though lost on the old road to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 運屬垂鴻，禮稽展慶。
