translations.literal: Our fortune aligned with the hanging great swan; rites must be examined to unfold celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Now fortune aligns with the great swan descending; rites must be observed to unfold our celebration.

sentences.zh: 大朝化覃無外，度豁包荒，山不謝乎纖埃，海不辭於支派。

translations.literal: The Great Court's transforming influence extends without exclusion; its magnanimity embraces the wilds—mountains do not decline the finest dust; seas do not reject the smallest branch.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Court's civilizing influence extends without exclusion; its magnanimity embraces the wilds. Mountains do not refuse the finest dust; seas do not reject the smallest stream.

sentences.zh: 謹當遵尋通道，遄赴稿街，但茲千里之傳聞，恐匪重霄之紆眷。

translations.literal: We shall strictly follow the established passage and hasten to the executioner's post—but this thousand-li report may not match the multilayered heavens' bent regard.
translations.idiomatic: We shall strictly follow the established route and hasten to present ourselves—but this report from a thousand li away may not match the multilayered heavens' gracious attention.

sentences.zh: 今以公狀附真、萬西遷，俟得報音，即備禮朝貢。」

translations.literal: Now we attach this official letter with Zhen and Wan moving westward; awaiting word in reply, we shall then prepare ritual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: We now send this official letter with Zhen and Wan traveling westward. Upon receiving your reply, we shall prepare ritual tribute.

sentences.zh: 徽又自言嘗夢至中華，作詩紀其事。

translations.literal: Closing the dispatch, Hui also said of his own accord that he had once dreamed he reached China and composed a poem to record the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Hui also reported that he had once dreamed of reaching China and composed a poem to commemorate it.

sentences.zh: 三年，拯以聞，朝廷議者亦謂可結之以謀契丹，神宗許焉，命拯諭以供擬腆厚之意。

translations.literal: In the third year, Cheng reported it; court discussants also said they could ally with Goryeo to scheme against the Khitan; Emperor Shenzong assented and ordered Cheng to instruct them with intent to supply and bestow richly.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Luo Cheng reported the dispatch. Court officials argued that an alliance with Goryeo could be used against the Khitan. Emperor Shenzong agreed and ordered Cheng to convey the court's intent to supply and bestow gifts generously.

sentences.zh: 徽遂遣民官侍郎金悌等百十人來，詔待之如夏國使。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon sent the Civil Affairs Vice Director Kim Ti and more than a hundred and ten others; an edict ordered they be received as envoys from Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then sent Kim Ti, Vice Director of Civil Affairs, with more than 110 others. The court ordered they be received with the same honors as envoys from Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 往時高麗人往反皆自登州，七年，遣其臣金良鑒來言，欲遠契丹，乞改塗由明州詣闕，從之。

translations.literal: Formerly Goryeo people going and coming all traveled through Deng Prefecture; in the seventh year he sent his minister Kim Yangjian to say they wished to keep distant from the Khitan and begged to change the route to proceed to court through Ming Prefecture; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Goryeo envoys had all traveled through Deng Prefecture. In the seventh year, Hui sent his minister Kim Yangjian to request a route avoiding Khitan territory, asking to travel through Ming Prefecture to reach court. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 郡縣供頓無舊准，頗擾民，詔立式頒下，費悉官給。

translations.literal: The counties' provisions for hosting had no old standard and greatly troubled the people; an edict established a model and promulgated it—the expenses all provided by the state.
translations.idiomatic: County provisions for hosting envoys had no established standard and greatly burdened the populace. The court established regulations and promulgated them, with all expenses paid from state funds.

sentences.zh: 又以其不邇華言，恐規利者私與交關，令所至禁止。

translations.literal: Also, because they did not understand Chinese speech, fearing that schemers for profit would privately engage in dealings with them, they were ordered prohibited wherever they passed.
translations.idiomatic: Because the envoys did not understand Chinese, the court also feared that profiteers might engage in private dealings with them and ordered such contact prohibited wherever they traveled.

sentences.zh: 徽問遺二府甚厚，詔以付市易務售縑帛答之。

translations.literal: Hui's inquiries and gifts to the Two Offices were very generous; an edict ordered them handed to the Market Exchange Office to sell silk and satin in return.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent lavish inquiries and gifts to the Two Offices. The court ordered the items consigned to the Market Exchange Office, which sold silk and satin to reciprocate.

sentences.zh: 又表求醫藥、畫塑之工以教國人，詔羅拯募願行者。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting physicians, pharmacists, and artisans in painting and sculpture to instruct his people; an edict ordered Luo Zhen to recruit those willing to go.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned for physicians, pharmacists, and masters of painting and sculpture to teach his people. The court ordered Luo Zhen to recruit volunteers.

sentences.zh: 九年，復遣崔思訓來，命中貴人仿都亭西驛例治館，待之寢厚，其使來者亦益多。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he again sent Cui Sihun to come; the court ordered palace eunuchs to establish a hostel following the precedent of the Western Hostel at Duting, treating them with growing generosity, and their envoys came in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Hui again sent Cui Sihun. The court ordered palace eunuchs to build a guesthouse on the model of the Western Hostel at Duting and treated the mission with increasing generosity. Envoys from Goryeo thereafter came in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻伶官十餘輩，曰：「夷樂無足觀，止欲潤色國史爾。」

translations.literal: Once he presented more than ten musical performers, saying: 'Barbarian music is not worth viewing—we only wish to ornament our national histories.'
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he presented more than ten musicians, explaining: 'Barbarian music is hardly worth watching; we only wish to enrich our national chronicles.'

sentences.zh: 帝以其國尚文，每賜書詔，必選詞臣著撰而擇其善者。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because their state esteemed literature, whenever bestowing written edicts always selected literary officials to compose drafts and chose the finest.
translations.idiomatic: Because Goryeo prized literary culture, whenever the Emperor issued written edicts he had literary officials draft several versions and chose the best.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣王舜封挾醫往診治。

translations.literal: In the second year, Wang Shunfeng was sent bringing physicians to treat and diagnose.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the court dispatched Wang Shunfeng with physicians to treat the king.

sentences.zh: 徽又使柳洪來謝，海中遇風，失所貢物。

translations.literal: Hui also sent Liu Hong to give thanks; on the sea they encountered wind and lost the tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: Hui also sent Liu Hong to express gratitude, but at sea they met a storm and lost the tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 洪上章自劾，敕書安慰。

translations.literal: Hong submitted a memorial impeaching himself; an edict letter comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong submitted a memorial accusing himself of failure. The Emperor replied with an edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 尋獻日本所造車，曰：「諸侯不貢車服，故不敢與土貢同進。」

translations.literal: Soon after he presented a carriage made in Japan, saying: 'Feudal lords do not present carriages and garments as tribute, so we dare not present it together with the regular land tribute.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he presented a carriage made in Japan, explaining: 'Feudal lords do not offer carriages and regalia as tribute, so we did not dare submit this together with our regular local tribute.'

sentences.zh: 前此貢物至。

translations.literal: When tribute goods arrived before this,
translations.idiomatic: Previously, whenever tribute goods arrived,

sentences.zh: 輒下有司估直，償以萬縑，至是命勿復估，以萬縑爲定數。

translations.literal: the court would always order the relevant offices to assess their value and compensate with ten thousand bolts of silk; now it was ordered not to assess again, with ten thousand bolts fixed as the set amount.
translations.idiomatic: the court had always ordered the relevant offices to appraise them and pay compensation of ten thousand bolts of silk. Now the court ordered that appraisals cease and fixed ten thousand bolts as the standard payment.

sentences.zh: 六年，徽卒，在位三十八年，治尚仁恕，爲東夷良主。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Hui died. He had reigned thirty-eight years; his governance favored leniency and forbearance, and he was regarded as a fine ruler among the Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Hui died. He had ruled thirty-eight years, governing with benevolence and forbearance, and was accounted a worthy sovereign among the eastern peoples.

sentences.zh: 然猶循其俗，王女不下嫁臣庶，必歸之兄弟，宗族貴臣亦然。

translations.literal: Yet he still followed their custom: kings' daughters did not marry commoners or subjects but had to be given to brothers; noble ministers of the lineage did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still followed their custom whereby royal daughters did not marry commoners or officials but were given in marriage to brothers, and the great clans observed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 次子運諫，以爲既通上國，宜以禮革故習。

translations.literal: His second son Yun remonstrated, holding that since they were now connected to the superior state, they ought to reform the old custom by ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Yun remonstrated, arguing that since they were now linked to the imperial court they ought to reform this old custom in accordance with proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 徽怒，斥之於外。

translations.literal: Hui was angry and expelled him abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was enraged and banished him from the realm.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，天子閔焉，詔明州修浮屠供一月，遣楊景略、王舜封祭奠，錢勰、宋球吊慰。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived, the Son of Heaven mourned him; an edict ordered Ming Prefecture to maintain Buddhist offerings for a month, and sent Yang Jinglüe and Wang Shunfeng to offer condolences, with Qian Wei and Song Qiu to convey condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, the Emperor mourned him. An edict ordered Ming Prefecture to sponsor Buddhist offerings for a month and dispatched Yang Jinglüe and Wang Shunfeng to offer condolences, with Qian Wei and Song Qiu to convey the court's sympathy.

sentences.zh: 景略辟李之儀書狀，帝以之儀文稱不著，宜得問學博洽、器宇整秀者召赴中書，試以文乃遣。

translations.literal: Jinglüe engaged Li Zhiyi as secretary; the Emperor considered that Zhiyi's literary reputation was not outstanding and that someone learned and widely versed, of dignified bearing and fine presence, should be summoned to the Secretariat for an examination by literary composition before dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglüe engaged Li Zhiyi as his secretary, but the Emperor judged Zhiyi's literary reputation insufficient and ordered that a scholar of broad learning and dignified bearing be summoned to the Secretariat for a literary examination before the mission could depart.

sentences.zh: 又以遠服不責其備，諭使者以相見之所殿名、鴟吻，皆聽勿避。

translations.literal: Also, because as a distant subject full display was not required, the envoys were instructed that in places of audience—hall names, owl-tail ornaments—all might be used without avoiding taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Because Goryeo was a distant tributary, the court also waived strict ceremonial requirements, instructing the envoys that at audience halls they need not avoid tabooed names or architectural ornaments such as owl-tail roof figures.

sentences.zh: 徽子順王勳嗣，百日卒。

translations.literal: Hui's son Shun Wang Xun succeeded; a hundred days later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's son Xun, titled Shun Wang, succeeded him but died within a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 弟宣王運嗣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xuan Wang Yun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yun, titled Xuan Wang, then took the throne.

sentences.zh: 運仁賢好文，內行飭備，每賈客市書至，則潔服焚香對之。

translations.literal: Yun was benevolent, worthy, and fond of literature; his private conduct was meticulous. Whenever merchant-traders brought books to market, he would bathe, change clothes, and burn incense before facing them.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was benevolent, worthy, and devoted to letters; his private conduct was exacting. Whenever merchants brought books for sale, he would bathe, change his garments, and burn incense before opening them.

sentences.zh: 八年，遣其弟僧統來朝，求問佛法並獻經像。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he sent his younger brother the monk Tong to court, requesting instruction in Buddhist dharma and presenting sutras and images.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, he sent his younger brother, the monk Tong, to court to seek instruction in Buddhist doctrine and to present sutras and images.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，遣使金上琦奉慰，林暨致賀，請市刑法之書、《太平御覽》、《開寶通禮》、《文苑英華》。

translations.literal: When Zhezong acceded, he sent the envoy Jin Shangqi to offer condolences and Lin Ji to offer congratulations, requesting to purchase books on penal law, the Taiping Imperial Reader, the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites, and the Literary Garden Anthology.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, Goryeo sent Jin Shangqi with condolences and Lin Ji with congratulations, requesting permission to buy works on penal law, the Taiping Imperial Reader, the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites, and the Literary Garden Anthology.

sentences.zh: 詔惟賜《文苑英華》一書，以名馬、錦綺、金帛報其禮。

translations.literal: An edict granted only the Literary Garden Anthology, replying to their courtesy with fine horses, brocade silks, gold, and silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted only the Literary Garden Anthology and reciprocated their courtesy with fine horses, brocades, gold, and silks.

sentences.zh: 運立四年卒，子懷王堯嗣。

translations.literal: Yun died after four years on the throne; his son Huai Wang Yao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yun died after four years on the throne. His son Yao, titled Huai Wang, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 未閱歲，以病不能爲國，國人請其叔父雞林公熙攝政。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed, because of illness he could not govern the state; the people asked his uncle the Cocklin Duke Xi to serve as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed, Yao fell ill and could not rule. The people asked his uncle Xi, Duke of Cocklin, to govern as regent.

sentences.zh: 未幾堯卒，熙乃立，凡數歲使不至。

translations.literal: Before long Yao died; Xi then took the throne. For several years envoys did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yao died and Xi assumed the throne himself. For several years no envoys came to court.

sentences.zh: 元祐四年，其王子義天使僧壽介至杭州祭亡僧，言國母使持二金塔爲兩宮壽，知州蘇軾奏卻之，語在《軾傳》。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyou, the prince Yishi sent the monk Shoujie to Hangzhou to perform rites for a deceased monk, saying the queen mother's envoys bore two gold pagodas as longevity gifts for the two palaces; Prefect Su Shi memorialized to refuse them—the account is in Shi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanyou, Prince Yishi sent the monk Shoujie to Hangzhou to perform rites for a deceased monk, claiming that the queen mother had sent two gold pagodas as longevity offerings for the two palaces. Prefect Su Shi memorialized to refuse them; the full account appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 熙後避遼主諱，改名顒。

translations.literal: Xi later avoided the taboo name of the Liao ruler and changed his name to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi later avoided the tabooed name of the Liao ruler and changed his name to Yong.

sentences.zh: 顒性貪吝，好奪商賈利，富室犯法，輒久縻責贖，雖微罪亦輸銀數斤。

translations.literal: Yong was greedy and miserly, fond of seizing merchants' profits; when wealthy households violated the law he would detain them long to exact ransom; even minor offenses required payment of several jin of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was greedy and grasping, ever seizing profit from merchants. When wealthy families ran afoul of the law he would hold them long to extract ransom, and even petty offenses required payment of several jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 五年，復通使，賜銀器五千兩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, envoys were again dispatched; five thousand liang of silver vessels were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, diplomatic contact resumed and the court bestowed five thousand liang of silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 七年，遣黃宗愨來獻《黃帝針經》，請市書甚衆。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Huang Zongque was sent presenting the Yellow Emperor's Canon of Acupuncture, and requested very many books.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Huang Zongque arrived bearing the Yellow Emperor's Canon of Acupuncture and requested a great many books.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書蘇軾言：「高麗入貢，無絲發利而有五害，今請諸書與收買金箔，皆宜勿許。」

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Su Shi said: 'Goryeo's tribute brings not a thread's worth of profit but five harms; now their requests for various books and for purchasing gold leaf should both be denied.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Su Shi argued: 'Goryeo's tribute yields not a thread of profit but five kinds of harm. Their requests for books and for purchasing gold leaf should both be refused.'

sentences.zh: 詔許買金箔，然卒市《冊府元龜》以歸。

translations.literal: An edict permitted buying gold leaf, yet they ultimately purchased the Prime Tortoise and returned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted the purchase of gold leaf, yet the envoys ultimately bought the Prime Tortoise and took it home.

sentences.zh: 元符中，遣士賓貢。

translations.literal: During Yuanfu, scholars were sent as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfu era, Goryeo sent scholars as tribute.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，遣任懿、王嘏來吊賀。

translations.literal: When Huizong acceded, he sent Ren Yi and Wang Jia to offer mourning and congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, Goryeo sent Ren Yi and Wang Jia with condolences and congratulations.

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，詔戶部侍郎劉逵、給事中吳拭往使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning, an edict ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Liu Kui and Vice Director of the Personnel Section Wu Shi to go as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongning, the court ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Liu Kui and Vice Director Wu Shi of the Personnel Section to serve as envoys.

sentences.zh: 顒卒，子俁嗣。

translations.literal: Yong died; his son Hou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yong died and was succeeded by his son Hou.

sentences.zh: 貢使接踵，且令士子金瑞等五人入太學，朝廷爲置博士。

translations.literal: Tribute envoys came in unbroken succession, and he also sent five scholars including Jin Rui to enter the Imperial University; the court appointed a Erudite for them.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions arrived one after another. Hou also sent five scholars, including Jin Rui, to enroll in the Imperial University, and the court appointed an Erudite to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 政和中，升其使爲國信，禮在夏國上，與遼人皆隸樞密院；

translations.literal: During the Zhenghe period, their missions were promoted to credentialed state envoys, ceremonial precedence above Xia, and together with Liao personnel were placed under the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe period, Goryeo missions were elevated to credentialed state envoys with ceremonial precedence above Western Xia. Together with Liao envoys they were placed under the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 改引伴、押伴官爲接送館伴。

translations.literal: the titles Guide and Escort officials were changed to Reception and Escort Hosts.
translations.idiomatic: and the offices of Guide and Escort Commissioner were renamed Reception and Escort Host.

sentences.zh: 賜以《大晟燕樂》、籩豆、簠簋、尊罍等器，至宴使者于睿謨殿中。

translations.literal: They were granted the Grand Flourishing Banquet Music, ritual vessels of baskets, beans, square and round grain vessels, wine vessels, and the like, and envoys were banqueted in the Hall of Sagacious Design.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted them the Grand Flourishing Banquet Music and ritual vessels—baskets, beans, grain vessels, and wine cups—and entertained envoys in the Hall of Sagacious Design.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，俁卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, Hou died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, Hou died.

sentences.zh: 初，高麗俗兄終弟及，至是諸弟爭立，其相李資深立俁子楷。

translations.literal: Initially, Goryeo custom was that when an elder brother died a younger brother succeeded; at this time younger brothers contended for the throne, and the minister Li Zishen installed Hou's son Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo had long followed fraternal succession, but now younger brothers fought over the throne until Minister Li Zishen installed Hou's son Kai.

sentences.zh: 來告哀，詔給事中路允迪、中書舍人傅墨卿奠慰。

translations.literal: They came to announce mourning; an edict ordered Minister of Verification Lu Yundi and Palace Secretarial Draftsman Fu Moqing to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to announce mourning, the court ordered Minister of Verification Lu Yundi and Secretariat Drafter Fu Moqing to convey condolences.

sentences.zh: 俁之在位也，求醫於朝，詔使二醫往，留二年而歸，楷語之曰：「聞朝廷將用兵伐遼。

translations.literal: During Hou's reign he sought physicians from the court; an edict sent two physicians who stayed two years before returning. Kai said to them: 'We hear the court is about to raise troops to attack Liao.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou's reign he had requested physicians from the Song court; two were sent and remained two years. On their return Kai told them: 'We hear your court is preparing to march against Liao.

sentences.zh: 遼兄弟之國，存之足爲邊捍。

translations.literal: Liao is a fraternal state; preserving it suffices as a border shield.
translations.idiomatic: Liao is a brother kingdom to yours. Keeping it intact is enough to shield your borders.

sentences.zh: 女真狼虎耳，不可交也。

translations.literal: The Jurchens are wolves and tigers—they cannot be befriended.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens are wolves and tigers. They are not a power you should court.

sentences.zh: 業已然，願二醫歸報天子，宜早爲備。」

translations.literal: The affair is already decided; I hope you two physicians will return and report to the Son of Heaven that he should prepare early.'
translations.idiomatic: The matter is already settled. I ask you both to return and tell the Son of Heaven to prepare without delay.'

sentences.zh: 歸奏其言，已無及矣。

translations.literal: When they returned and reported his words, it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned and reported his warning, it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，賀使至明州，御史胡舜陟言：「高麗靡敝國家五十年，政和以來，人使歲至，淮、浙之間苦之。

translations.literal: When Qinzong acceded, congratulatory envoys reached Ming Prefecture; Censor Hu Shunzhi said: 'Goryeo has exhausted the state for fifty years; since Zhenghe envoys have come every year, and the Huai and Zhe regions have suffered for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong took the throne, congratulatory envoys reached Ming Prefecture. Censor Hu Shunzhi argued: 'For fifty years Goryeo has drained our resources. Since the Zhenghe era their envoys have come every year, and the Huai and Zhe circuits have borne the burden.

sentences.zh: 彼昔臣事契丹，今必事金國，安知不窺我虛實以報，宜止勿使來。」

translations.literal: They once served the Khitan and will surely now serve the Jin state—how do we know they will not spy out our weaknesses to report? They should be stopped from coming.'
translations.idiomatic: They once served the Khitan and will surely serve the Jin now. Who is to say they will not probe our weaknesses and report back? Their missions should be halted.'

sentences.zh: 乃詔留館於明而納其贄幣。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered them lodged at Ming Prefecture while accepting their tribute gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered the envoys detained at Ming Prefecture while accepting their tribute gifts.

sentences.zh: 明年始歸國。

translations.literal: The following year they were allowed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they were permitted to return home.

sentences.zh: 自王微以降，雖通使不絕，然受契丹封冊，奉其正朔，上朝廷及他文書，蓋有稱甲子者。

translations.literal: From Wang Hui onward, though envoys never ceased, they received Khitan investiture and seals and observed their calendar; in documents to the imperial court and elsewhere some used the sexagenary cycle dating.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Hui onward, although missions to the Song never ceased, Goryeo accepted Khitan investiture and observed the Liao calendar. In documents to the Song court and elsewhere they sometimes dated entries by the sexagenary cycle alone.

sentences.zh: 歲貢契丹至於六，而誅求不已。

translations.literal: Annual tribute to the Khitan reached six missions, yet demands never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They sent as many as six tribute missions a year to the Khitan, yet Liao demands never ceased.

sentences.zh: 常云：「高麗乃我奴耳，南朝何以厚待之？」

translations.literal: They would often say: 'Goryeo is but our slave—why does the Southern Court treat them so generously?'
translations.idiomatic: Liao envoys would often declare: 'Goryeo is nothing but our slave—why does the Southern Court treat them so lavishly?'

sentences.zh: 使至其國，尤倨暴，館伴及公卿小失意，輒行ㄏ棰，聞我使至，必假他事來覘，分取賜物。

translations.literal: When envoys reached their state they were especially arrogant and violent; hosts and even minor officials who displeased them would be beaten with cudgels; when they heard our envoys were coming they would surely find some pretext to observe them and divide the gifts taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao envoys reached Goryeo they were brutally overbearing; hosts and even junior officials who displeased them were beaten with clubs. Learning that Song envoys were coming, they would contrive pretexts to observe them and seize a share of the gifts.

sentences.zh: 嘗詰其西向修貢事，高麗表謝，其略曰：「中國，三甲子方得一朝；

translations.literal: They once questioned them about submitting tribute westward; Goryeo memorialized in apology, the gist being: 'The Central Court—only one audience in three sexagenary cycles;
translations.idiomatic: Liao once challenged Goryeo for sending tribute westward. Goryeo replied in a memorial whose gist ran: 'The Central Court grants an audience only once in three sexagenary cycles;

sentences.zh: 大邦，一周天每修六貢。」

translations.literal: the great power—six tributes every celestial revolution.'
translations.idiomatic: your great state requires six tributes every full cycle of heaven.'

sentences.zh: 契丹悟，乃得免。

translations.literal: The Khitan understood and they were then exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan understood the point and thereafter eased their demands.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，慮金人通於高麗，命迪功郎胡蠡假宗正少卿爲高麗國使以間之。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, fearing the Jin people would contact Goryeo, he appointed Acting Merit Officer Hu Li, bearing the false title of Vice Director of the Imperial Clan, as envoy to Goryeo to probe them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, fearing Jin contact with Goryeo, he appointed Acting Merit Officer Hu Li, with the nominal title of Vice Director of the Imperial Clan, to go to Goryeo and sound them out.

sentences.zh: 蠡之回，史失書。

translations.literal: When Li returned, the history failed to record it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Li returned, the historians failed to record his mission.

sentences.zh: 二年，浙東路馬步軍都總管楊應誠上言：「由高麗至女真路甚徑，請身使三韓，結雞林以圖迎二聖。」

translations.literal: In the second year, Grand Commander of Horse and Foot Forces on the Zhedong Circuit Yang Yingcheng memorialized: 'The route from Goryeo to the Jurchens is very direct; I request to go in person to the Three Han, ally with Cocklin to plan welcoming the Two Sages.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Yang Yingcheng, Grand Commander of Horse and Foot on the Zhedong Circuit, memorialized: 'The route from Goryeo to the Jurchens is very short. I ask to go myself to the Three Han and ally with Cocklin to plan the recovery of the Two Sages.'

sentences.zh: 乃以應誠假刑部尚書充高麗國信使。

translations.literal: He was then made Acting Minister of Punishments and Credentialed Envoy to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon appointed Acting Minister of Punishments and Credentialed Envoy to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 浙東帥臣翟汝文奏言：「應誠欺罔，爲身謀耳。

translations.literal: Commander of Zhedong Zhai Ruwen memorialized: 'Yingcheng deceives and misleads—this is a plan for himself alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhedong commander Zhai Ruwen countered: 'Yingcheng is deceiving the court—this scheme serves only himself.

sentences.zh: 若高麗辭以金人亦請問津以窺吳、越，其將何辭以對？

translations.literal: If Goryeo refuses on the grounds that the Jin also request passage to spy on Wu and Yue, what words will he have to answer?
translations.idiomatic: If Goryeo refuses on the grounds that the Jin also seek passage to spy on Wu and Yue, what answer will he give?

sentences.zh: 萬一辱命，取笑遠夷，願毋遣。」

translations.literal: Should he by any chance be dishonored, he would bring ridicule from distant barbarians—I pray he not be sent.'
translations.idiomatic: If he is disgraced abroad, the court will be mocked by distant peoples. I beg that he not be dispatched.'

sentences.zh: 應誠聞之，遂與副使韓衍、書狀官孟健由杭州浮海以行。

translations.literal: Yingcheng heard this and proceeded anyway, with Vice-envoy Han Yan and secretary Meng Jian, traveling from Hangzhou by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Yingcheng heard the protest but set out anyway with Vice-envoy Han Yan and secretary Meng Jian, sailing from Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，抵高麗，諭其王楷以所欲爲，楷曰：「大朝自有山東路，盍不由登州往？」

translations.literal: In the sixth month they reached Goryeo and urged King Kai to do as desired; Kai said: 'The great court has its own Shandong route—why not go via Dengzhou?'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they reached Goryeo and pressed King Kai to cooperate. Kai replied: 'The great court has its own Shandong route—why not travel through Dengzhou?'

sentences.zh: 應誠曰：「以貴國路徑耳。」

translations.literal: Yingcheng said: 'Because your country's route is the shorter.'
translations.idiomatic: Yingcheng answered: 'Because the route through your country is shorter.'

sentences.zh: 楷有難色，已而命其門下侍郎傳佾至館中，果對如翟汝文言。

translations.literal: Kai looked troubled; soon he ordered his Vice Director of the Secretariat Fu Yi to the hostel, and the reply was indeed as Zhai Ruwen had said.
translations.idiomatic: Kai hesitated, then sent his Vice Director of the Secretariat, Fu Yi, to the hostel with the very objections Zhai Ruwen had predicted.

sentences.zh: 應誠曰：「女真不善水戰。」

translations.literal: Yingcheng said: 'The Jurchens are not skilled at naval warfare.'
translations.idiomatic: Yingcheng insisted: 'The Jurchens are poor fighters at sea.'

sentences.zh: 佾曰：「彼常於海道往來，況女真舊臣本國，今反臣事之，其強弱可見矣。」

translations.literal: Yi said: 'They constantly travel the sea lanes; moreover the Jurchens were formerly subjects of our state and now in turn serve them—their strength or weakness is evident.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yi replied: 'They constantly use the sea routes. Moreover, the Jurchens were once our subjects and now serve the Jin in turn—their strength is plain to see.'

sentences.zh: 居數日，復遣其中書侍郎崔洪宰、知樞密院金富軾持前議不變，謂二聖今在燕雲，大朝雖盡納土，未必可得，何不練兵與戰？

translations.literal: After several days they again sent their Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Hongzai and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Jin Fushi, holding to the previous position unchanged, saying the Two Sages were now in Yan-Yun, and that even if the great court yielded all territory they might not be recovered—why not train troops and fight?
translations.idiomatic: Several days later they sent Vice Director Cui Hongzai and Vice Commissioner Jin Fushi with the same refusal, arguing that the Two Sages were now in Yan-Yun and that even if the Song surrendered every inch of territory they might not be recovered—why not train troops and fight instead?

sentences.zh: 終不奉詔。

translations.literal: They ultimately would not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: They would not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 應誠留兩月餘，不得已見楷于壽昌門，受其拜表而還。

translations.literal: Yingcheng remained more than two months; with no alternative he met Kai at Shouchang Gate, received his memorial of obeisance and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yingcheng lingered more than two months. At last, with no other option, he met Kai at Shouchang Gate, received his memorial of obeisance, and sailed home.

sentences.zh: 十月，至闕，入對言狀，上以楷負國恩，怒甚。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached court, entered audience and reported; the Emperor, because Kai had betrayed imperial grace, was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached court and reported. The Emperor, believing Kai had betrayed imperial favor, was furious.

sentences.zh: 尚書右丞朱勝非曰：「彼鄰金人，與中國隔海，利害甚明。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Right Zhu Shengfei said: 'They border the Jin people and are separated from China by the sea—the advantage and harm are very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhu Shengfei said: 'They border the Jin and are separated from us by the sea. The balance of advantage is obvious.

sentences.zh: 曩時待之過厚，今安能責其報也。」

translations.literal: In former times we treated them too generously—how can we now demand repayment?'
translations.idiomatic: We once treated them too generously. How can we now demand loyalty in return?'

sentences.zh: 右僕射黃潛善曰：「以巨艦載精兵數萬，徑搗其國，彼寧不懼。」

translations.literal: Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Huang Qianshan said: 'Load great warships with tens of thousands of picked troops and strike their country directly—they would surely fear.'
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Huang Qianshan urged: 'Send great warships loaded with tens of thousands of elite troops straight against their country—they would surely tremble.'

sentences.zh: 勝非曰：「越海興師，燕山之事可爲近鑒。」

translations.literal: Shengfei said: 'Cross-sea campaigns—the affair at Yanshan can serve as a recent mirror.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei rejoined: 'A war across the sea? The Yanshan campaign is warning enough.'

sentences.zh: 上怒解。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger eased.

sentences.zh: 十一月，楷遣其臣尹彥頤奉表謝罪，詔以二聖未歸，燕設不宜用樂，乃設幕殿門外，命客省官吳得興伴賜酒食，命中書舍人張澂押伴，如禮遣還。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Kai sent his minister Yin Yanzi with a memorial apologizing; an edict said that because the Two Sages had not returned, music was inappropriate at the Yan feast, so a tent-hall was set up outside the palace gate; Guest Relations Officer Wu Dexing was ordered to accompany the gift of wine and food; Secretariat Drafter Zhang Cheng was appointed Escort Host and they were sent back according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Kai sent his minister Yin Yanzi with a letter of apology. Because the Two Sages had not returned, the court ruled that music was inappropriate at the Yan feast and instead set up a pavilion outside the palace gate. Guest Relations Officer Wu Dexing was ordered to present wine and food, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Cheng was named Escort Host, and the envoys were sent home with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，上謂輔臣曰：「聞上皇遣內臣、宮女各二人隨高麗貢使來，朕聞之悲喜交集。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year the Emperor told his chief ministers: 'I hear that the Retired Emperor has sent two inner eunuchs and two palace women with the Goryeo tribute envoys—I am both glad and sad on hearing this.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year the Emperor told his chief ministers: 'I hear that the Retired Emperor has sent two inner eunuchs and two palace women with the Goryeo tribute mission. The news fills me with mingled joy and grief.'

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩曰：「此必金人之意，不然高麗必不敢，安知非窺我虛實以報。」

translations.literal: Lü Yihao said: 'This must be the Jin people's idea; otherwise Goryeo would never dare—how do we know they are not spying our condition to report?'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yihao said: 'This must be the Jin people's doing. Otherwise Goryeo would never dare. Who can say they are not probing our condition to report back?'

sentences.zh: 於是詔止之，略曰：「王緬守基圖，夙同文軌，乃附乘桴之信，嗣修貢篚之恭。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict halted it, in summary: 'The king guards his foundation; from of old we share the same culture; he again shows faith in crossing by raft and continues the tribute-basket's respect.
translations.idiomatic: The court then issued an edict halting the mission. Its gist read: 'The king guards his patrimony; from of old our cultures have run together. He again trusts the crossing by raft and renews the tribute-basket's courtesy.

sentences.zh: 惟忠順之無他，質神明而靡愧，屬關聞聽，良用歎嘉。

translations.literal: His loyalty alone and no other is attested before the spirits without shame; I have heard the report with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty alone, attested before heaven, moves us without shame. We have heard the report with admiration.

sentences.zh: 言念晚年，實爲多故，舉中原之生聚，遭強敵之震驚，既涉境以冞深，猶稱兵而未已，茲移仗衛，暫駐江湖。

translations.literal: Thinking of his later years in many troubles—the multitude of the central plains caught in the shock of a fierce enemy, having crossed the border deeper and deeper, yet calling out troops without cease—now moving the imperial guard temporarily to the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: We think of his later years in turmoil—the people of the central plains shaken by a fierce enemy, the border crisis deepening day by day, yet war cries unceasing, while the imperial guard has withdrawn for a time to the rivers and lakes.

sentences.zh: 如行使之果來，恐有司之不戒，俟休邊警，當問聘期。

translations.literal: If your mission should truly come, I fear our offices will not be on guard; wait until the border alarm eases, then we may set the date for envoys.
translations.idiomatic: If your embassy should truly arrive, I fear our officials will not be vigilant. Wait until the border alarm subsides, and we shall fix a date for envoys.

sentences.zh: 壞晉館以納車，庶無後悔，閉漢關而謝質，非用前規。

translations.literal: Destroy the Jin hostel to receive the carriage—lest there be later regret; close the Han pass and decline the hostage—not following former rules.
translations.idiomatic: Tear down the Jin guesthouse rather than receive your carriage, lest we regret it later. Close the Han frontier and refuse your hostage—that is not the old practice, but necessity demands it.

sentences.zh: 想彼素懷，知吾誠意。」

translations.literal: Consider that their long-held sentiment will know our sincere intent.'
translations.idiomatic: We trust that your long-standing goodwill will understand our sincere intent.'

sentences.zh: 紹興元年十月，高麗將入貢，禮部侍郎柳約言：「四明殘破之余，荒蕪單弱，恐起戎心，宜屯重兵以俟其至。」

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Shaoxing, as Goryeo was about to enter tribute, Vice Minister of Rites Liu Yue said: 'Beyond the ruins of Siming, desolate and weak alone, I fear this may stir barbarian ambition—heavy troops should be stationed awaiting their arrival.'
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Shaoxing, as Goryeo was preparing to send tribute, Vice Minister of Rites Liu Yue warned: 'Siming lies in ruins, desolate and defenseless. I fear this may invite barbarian ambition. Heavy troops should be stationed to await their arrival.'

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔柳約奉使高麗，不果行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict ordered Liu Yue to serve as envoy to Goryeo; the mission did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict appointed Liu Yue envoy to Goryeo, but the mission never sailed.

sentences.zh: 二年閏四月，楷遣其禮部員外郎崔惟清、閣門祗候沈起入貢金百兩、銀千兩、綾羅二百匹、人參五百斤，惟清所獻亦三之一。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of the second year, Kai sent his Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites Cui Weiqing and Gate Attendant Shen Qi to offer tribute of a hundred liang of gold, a thousand liang of silver, two hundred bolts of silk gauze, and five hundred jin of ginseng; Weiqing's personal gifts were also one-third of that.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of the second year, Kai sent Vice Director of Rites Cui Weiqing and Gate Attendant Shen Qi with tribute of one hundred liang of gold, one thousand liang of silver, two hundred bolts of silk gauze, and five hundred jin of ginseng. Weiqing's personal gifts amounted to one-third of the same.

sentences.zh: 上御後殿引見，賜惟清、起金帶二，答以溫詔遣還。

translations.literal: The Emperor received them in audience in the rear hall, bestowed on Weiqing and Qi two gold belts each, and sent them back with a warm edict in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received them in the rear hall, bestowed a gold belt on each, and sent them home with a gracious reply edict.

sentences.zh: 是月，定海縣言，民亡入高麗者約八十人，願奉表還國。

translations.literal: That month Dinghai County reported that about eighty people among the populace who had fled to Goryeo wished to present a memorial and return home.
translations.idiomatic: That month Dinghai County reported that some eighty subjects who had fled to Goryeo wished to submit a memorial and return home.

sentences.zh: 詔候到日，高麗綱首卓榮等量與推恩。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that when they arrived, the Goryeo convoy chief Zhuo Rong and others should grant them proportional imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that when they arrived, the Goryeo convoy chief Zhuo Rong and others should extend proportional imperial favors.

sentences.zh: 十二月，聞高麗遣知樞密院事洪彝敘等六十五人來貢，議以臨安府學館其使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month it was learned that Goryeo sent Vice Commissioner Hong Yixu and sixty-five others to offer tribute; discussion favored lodging them at the Lin'an Prefecture school.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the court learned that Goryeo had sent Vice Commissioner Hong Yixu with sixty-five others bearing tribute. Officials proposed housing them at the Lin'an Prefecture school.

sentences.zh: 言者謂雖在兵間，不可無學，恐爲所窺。

translations.literal: Memorialists said that even amid warfare one must not be without learning, for fear they would spy it out.
translations.idiomatic: Critics objected that even in wartime the state must not neglect learning, lest the envoys spy out its strengths.

sentences.zh: 詔以法惠寺爲同文館以待之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Fahui Temple be made the Tongwen Lodge to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The court decreed that Fahui Temple should serve as the Tongwen Lodge to receive the envoys.

sentences.zh: 既而卒不至。

translations.literal: Before long they in the end did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they never arrived.

sentences.zh: 六年，高麗持牒官金稚圭至明州，賜銀帛遣之，懼其爲金間也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Goryeo's credential-bearing official Jin Zhigui arrived at Mingzhou; silver and silks were bestowed and he was sent away, for fear he was a Jin spy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shaoxing, Goryeo's credential officer Jin Zhigui reached Mingzhou. The court gave him silver and silks and sent him home, fearing he was acting as a Jin agent.

sentences.zh: 三十二年三月，高麗綱首徐德榮詣明州言，本國欲遣賀使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-second year, Goryeo's convoy chief Xu Derong went to Mingzhou and said that his country wished to send congratulatory envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, the Goryeo convoy leader Xu Derong came to Mingzhou and reported that his kingdom intended to dispatch envoys to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 守臣韓仲通以聞，殿中侍御史吳芾奏曰：「高麗與金人接壤，昔稚圭之來，朝廷懼其爲間，亟遣還。

translations.literal: The defending official Han Zhongtong reported it; Palace Attendant Censor Wu Fei memorialized, saying: 'Goryeo borders the Jin people; when Zhigui came before, the court feared he was a spy and quickly sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural defender Han Zhongtong reported the matter upward. Palace Attendant Censor Wu Fei submitted a memorial: "Goryeo shares a border with the Jin. When Jin Zhigui came earlier, the court suspected he was a spy and hurried him back at once.

sentences.zh: 今兩國交兵，德榮之請，得無可疑？

translations.literal: Now the two states are at war—is Derong's request not open to suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: Now the two powers are at war. Can Xu Derong's request be anything but suspect?

sentences.zh: 使其果來，猶恐不測，萬一不至，貽笑遠方。」

translations.literal: If they should truly come, one still fears the unpredictable; if by any chance they do not come, one brings ridicule from afar.'
translations.idiomatic: If they do come, we may still face unforeseen trouble; if they fail to come after all, we will be mocked in distant lands."

sentences.zh: 詔止之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put a stop to the plan.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年四月，明州言高麗入貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Longxing, Mingzhou reported that Goryeo was entering tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Longxing (1164), Mingzhou reported that Goryeo was sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 史不書引見日，恐同彝敘之詐。

translations.literal: The history does not record the day of audience, for fear of fraud like Yixu's.
translations.idiomatic: The annals do not record the day they were received in audience, lest the episode repeat the deception of Hong Yixu's mission.

sentences.zh: 其後使命遂絕。

translations.literal: After that, missions then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After that, embassies between the two courts ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 慶元間，詔禁商人持銅錢入高麗，蓋絕之也。

translations.literal: During the Qingyuan period, an edict forbade merchants to carry copper cash into Goryeo—this was to cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingyuan era, an edict barred merchants from taking copper coin into Goryeo, a measure meant to sever ties altogether.

sentences.zh: 初，高麗入使，明、越困於供給，朝廷館遇燕齎錫予之費以钜萬計，饋其主者不在焉。

translations.literal: At first, when Goryeo envoys entered, Ming and Yue were strained by provisioning; the court's costs for lodging, feasting, travel allowances, and bestowals ran to tens of thousands, not counting gifts to their ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo missions first arrived, Mingzhou and Yuezhou were worn down supplying them. Court expenses for lodging, banquets, travel stipends, and gifts ran into the tens of thousands—and that did not include what was sent to the Goryeo king.

sentences.zh: 我使之行，每乘二神舟，費亦不貲。

translations.literal: When our envoys went, they each took two divine ships; the cost was likewise not small.
translations.idiomatic: Song embassies sailed on two state vessels apiece, and their costs were no less ruinous.

sentences.zh: 三節官吏縻爵捐廩，皆仰縣官。

translations.literal: The officials of the Three Festivals were tied to ranks and stipends, all relying on the county treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Officials attached to the Three Festival embassies held titular ranks and drew salaries, all of it charged to local government.

sentences.zh: 昔蘇軾言於先朝，謂高麗入貢有五害，以此也。

translations.literal: Formerly Su Shi spoke to the previous court, saying that Goryeo's entering tribute had five harms—this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi had once warned the former court that Goryeo tribute carried five great harms; this was exactly what he meant.

sentences.zh: 惟是國于吳會，事異東都。

translations.literal: Only this state was in the Wu-Hui region; the matter differed from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the dynasty now sat in the Wu-Hui heartland, and the situation differed from the days of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 昔高麗入使，率由登、萊，山河之限甚遠，今直趨四明，四明距行都限一浙水耳。

translations.literal: Formerly Goryeo envoys mostly came by Deng and Lai; the barrier of mountains and rivers was very far. Now they go straight to Siming; Siming is separated from the traveling capital only by one stretch of Zhe waters.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times Goryeo envoys usually entered through Dengzhou and Laizhou, separated from the capital by vast mountains and rivers. Now they sailed straight to Siming, which lay only a single crossing of the Zhe River from the moving court.

sentences.zh: 由海道奉使高麗，彌漫汪洋，洲嶼險阻，遇黑風，舟觸礁輒敗，出急水門至群山島，始謂平達，非數十日不至也。

translations.literal: Going by sea route as envoy to Goryeo, the vast expanse of ocean and dangerous islets—meeting a black wind, a ship striking reefs would be wrecked; leaving the Urgent Water Gate for the cluster of mountain isles, one only then thought the way level and direct, yet not several tens of days would one fail to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The sea road to Goryeo crossed a boundless ocean strewn with perilous islets. A black gale could dash a ship on the reefs. Even after passing the Urgent Water Gate and reaching the archipelago of mountain islands, where the route seemed open at last, the voyage still required many tens of days.

sentences.zh: 舟南北行，遇順風則歷險如夷，至不數日。

translations.literal: When the ship went north or south and met a fair wind, it passed dangers as if on level ground, arriving in not several days.
translations.idiomatic: When the wind favored the course, north or south, the same voyage swept through the hazards as if over flat ground and could be finished in only a few days.

sentences.zh: 其國東西二千里，南北五百里，西北接契丹，恃鴨綠江以爲固，江廣三百步。

translations.literal: Their state was two thousand li east to west and five hundred li north to south; northwest it adjoined the Khitan, relying on the Yalu River as its defense—the river was three hundred paces wide.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom measured two thousand li from east to west and five hundred from north to south. On the northwest it bordered the Khitan, and its chief defense was the Yalu River, three hundred paces across.

sentences.zh: 其東所臨，海水清澈，下視十丈，東南望明州，水皆碧。

translations.literal: On the east where it faced the sea, the water was clear and one could see ten zhang down; looking southeast toward Mingzhou, the waters were all jade-green.
translations.idiomatic: Along its eastern coast the sea ran clear enough to see ten zhang below the surface. Toward the southeast, in the direction of Mingzhou, the water shone deep blue-green.

sentences.zh: 王居開州蜀莫郡，曰開成府。

translations.literal: The king dwelt in Kaizhou, Shumo Command, called Kaesong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The king resided at Kaesong in Shumo Command, known as Kaesong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 依大山置宮室，立城壁，名其山曰神嵩。

translations.literal: Relying on a great mountain he set palace halls and raised city walls, naming the mountain Divine Summit.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces and city walls rose against a great mountain the court named Divine Summit.

sentences.zh: 民居皆茅茨，大止兩椽，覆以瓦者才十二。

translations.literal: The people's dwellings were all thatched; at most two rafters, and those roofed with tile were only one in twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Common houses were thatched huts, rarely more than two bays wide, and scarcely one dwelling in twelve had a tiled roof.

sentences.zh: 以新羅爲東州樂浪府，號東京。

translations.literal: Silla was made East Prefecture, Langye Commandery, called the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The old Silla lands formed East Prefecture and Langye Commandery, styled the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 百濟爲金州金馬郡，號南京。

translations.literal: Baekje was Jin Prefecture, Jinma Commandery, called the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Former Baekje territory became Jin Prefecture and Jinma Commandery, called the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 平壤爲鎮州，號西京。

translations.literal: Pyongyang was Zhen Prefecture, called the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pyongyang served as Zhen Prefecture, the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 西京最盛。

translations.literal: The Western Capital was most prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three capitals, the Western Capital was the most flourishing.

sentences.zh: 總之，凡三京、四府、八牧、郡百有十八、縣鎮三百九十、洲島三千七百。

translations.literal: In total there were three capitals, four prefectures, eight mu, one hundred eighteen commanderies, three hundred ninety county-towns, and three thousand seven hundred islets.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether the realm counted three capitals, four superior prefectures, eight circuits, one hundred eighteen commanderies, three hundred ninety counties and towns, and three thousand seven hundred islands.

sentences.zh: 郡邑之小者，或只百家。

translations.literal: The smallest commanderies and towns might have only a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Some of the smallest districts held no more than a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 男女二百十萬口，兵、民、僧各居其一。

translations.literal: Men and women numbered two million one hundred thousand mouths; soldiers, commoners, and monks each occupied one third.
translations.idiomatic: The population stood at 2.1 million men and women, divided roughly into equal thirds of soldiers, civilians, and monks.

sentences.zh: 地寒多山，土宜松柏，有粳、黍、麻、麥而無秫，以粳爲酒。

translations.literal: The land was cold and mountainous; the soil suited pine and cypress. They had glutinous rice, millet, hemp, and wheat but no sorghum, and used glutinous rice to make wine.
translations.idiomatic: The country was cold and rugged, with soil that favored pine and cypress. Farmers grew glutinous rice, millet, hemp, and wheat but not sorghum, and they brewed their wine from glutinous rice.

sentences.zh: 少絲蠶，匹縑直銀十兩，多衣麻紵。

translations.literal: Silk worms were few; a bolt of silk gauze was worth ten liang of silver, and most wore hemp and ramie.
translations.idiomatic: Sericulture was scarce. A bolt of silk cost ten liang of silver, and most people dressed in hemp and ramie cloth.

sentences.zh: 王出，乘車駕牛，曆山險乃騎。

translations.literal: When the king went out, he rode in a cart drawn by oxen; only when the mountains grew perilous did he mount a horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the king traveled abroad, he rode in an ox-drawn cart and mounted a horse only where the mountain roads turned treacherous.

sentences.zh: 紫衣行前，捧《護國仁王經》以導。

translations.literal: Men in purple robes went before, holding the Scripture of the Nation-Protecting Benevolent King to lead the way.
translations.idiomatic: Purple-robed attendants walked ahead, bearing the Scripture of the Nation-Protecting Benevolent King as a guide.

sentences.zh: 出令曰教，曰宣。

translations.literal: Issued orders were called jiao and xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Royal orders went by the names jiao and xuan.

sentences.zh: 臣民呼之曰聖上，私謂曰嚴公，後妃曰宮主。

translations.literal: Subjects addressed him as Holy Lord; in private they called him the Severe Lord; consorts were called Palace Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects addressed the king as Holy Lord, though in private they called him the Severe Lord. Consorts were styled Palace Ladies.

sentences.zh: 百官名稱、階、勳、功臣、檢校，頗與中朝相類。

translations.literal: The titles, ranks, orders of merit, meritorious subjects, and inspector-general posts of the hundred officials were rather similar to the central court.
translations.idiomatic: Official titles, ranks, orders of merit, honors for meritorious service, and acting inspector posts all closely resembled those of the Song court.

sentences.zh: 過御史台則下馬，違者有劾。

translations.literal: Passing the Censorate one dismounted; violators were impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Officials dismounted when passing the Censorate, and anyone who failed to do so faced impeachment.

sentences.zh: 士人以族望相高，柳、崔、金、李四姓爲貴種。

translations.literal: Scholars esteemed one another by clan prestige; the four surnames Liu, Cui, Jin, and Li were noble lines.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars ranked one another by clan prestige. The surnames Liu, Cui, Jin, and Li were regarded as the noblest bloodlines.

sentences.zh: 無宦者，以世族子爲內侍六衛。

translations.literal: There were no eunuchs; sons of eminent clans served as inner attendants of the Six Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The court employed no eunuchs. Sons of great families served instead as inner attendants in the Six Guards.

sentences.zh: 歲十二月朔，王坐紫門小殿注官，外官則付國相。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month each year, the king sat in the Purple Gate small hall to assign offices; outer officials were entrusted to the state chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month the king took his seat in the small hall of the Purple Gate to appoint officials, while outer appointments were left to the state chancellor.

sentences.zh: 有國子監、四門學，學者六千人。

translations.literal: There were the Directorate of Education and the Four Gates Academy, with six thousand students.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Education and the Four Gates Academy enrolled six thousand students.

sentences.zh: 貢士三等，王城曰土貢，郡邑曰鄉貢，他國人曰賓貢。

translations.literal: Presented scholars had three grades: in the royal city they were called earth tribute, in commanderies and towns village tribute, and men of other states guest tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute scholars fell into three classes: capital candidates called earth tribute, provincial candidates called village tribute, and foreigners called guest tribute.

sentences.zh: 間歲試於所屬，再試於學，所取不過三四十人，然後王親試以詩、賦、論三題，謂之簾前重試。

translations.literal: In alternate years they were tested in their jurisdictions, tested again at the schools, and no more than thirty or forty were taken; then the king personally tested them on three topics—poetry, fu, and discourse—called the Curtain Re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Every other year candidates were examined in their home districts and tested again at the schools, of whom no more than thirty or forty were chosen. The king then examined them personally on poetry, fu, and expository essays in what was called the Curtain Re-examination.

sentences.zh: 亦有制科宏詞之目，然特文具而已。

translations.literal: There were also categories for special examinations and grand rhetoric, yet they were merely formal entries.
translations.idiomatic: Special examination tracks and grand-rhetoric categories also existed, but they were little more than paper formalities.

sentences.zh: 士尚聲律，少通經。

translations.literal: Scholars prized tonal rules; few mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars prized regulated verse and tonal craft; few were deeply versed in the classics.

sentences.zh: 王城有華人數百，多閩人因賈舶至者，密試其所能，誘以祿仕，或強留之終身，朝廷使至，有陳牒來訴者，則取以歸。

translations.literal: In the royal city were several hundred Chinese, mostly men of Min who had come on merchant ships; their abilities were secretly tested and they were lured with salary and office, or forcibly detained for life. When the court's envoys arrived, if any presented petitions appealing, they were taken back.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Chinese lived in the capital, most of them Fujianese who had arrived on trading ships. The court quietly tested their talents and tempted them with salaries and posts, sometimes detaining them for life. When a Song embassy came, any who filed petitions to return were reclaimed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 百官以米爲奉，皆給田，納祿半給，死乃拘之。

translations.literal: The hundred officials took rice as salary; all were granted fields, half the salary paid in kind, and at death it was seized back.
translations.idiomatic: Officials received their salaries in rice and were all granted fields. Half the stipend was paid in grain, and the land was reclaimed at death.

sentences.zh: 國無私田，民計口授業。

translations.literal: The state had no private fields; the people were allotted holdings by counted mouths.
translations.idiomatic: There was no private land in the kingdom. Fields were allotted to households according to the number of mouths.

sentences.zh: 十六以上則充軍，六軍三衛常留官府，三歲以選戍西北，半歲而更。

translations.literal: From sixteen upward one entered the army; the Six Armies and Three Guards constantly remained at government offices; every three years men were chosen to garrison the northwest, rotating at half-year intervals.
translations.idiomatic: Men sixteen and older were conscripted. The Six Armies and Three Guards were permanently stationed at government posts, while every three years selected troops rotated to garrison the northwest for half a year at a time.

sentences.zh: 有警則執兵，任事則服勞，事已復歸農畝。

translations.literal: When there was an alarm they took up arms; when assigned duties they performed labor; when the task was done they returned again to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: In an emergency they took up arms; when called to duty they performed labor; when the task ended they went back to the fields.

sentences.zh: 王亦有分地以供私用，王母、妃主、世子皆受湯沐田。

translations.literal: The king also had allotted lands for private use; the queen mother, consorts, and crown prince all received bath-fief fields.
translations.idiomatic: The king held allotted lands for his private expenses. The queen mother, consorts, and crown prince each received bath-fief estates for their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 上下以賈販利入爲事。

translations.literal: Above and below took profit from trade and peddling as their business.
translations.idiomatic: From the throne to the common people, profit from trade was the lifeblood of daily affairs.

sentences.zh: 日中爲虛，用米布貿易。

translations.literal: At midday the market stood empty; they used rice and cloth in trade.
translations.idiomatic: Markets stood empty at midday, and people traded in rice and cloth.

sentences.zh: 地產銅，不知鑄錢，中國所予錢，藏之府庫，時出傳玩而已。

translations.literal: The land produced copper but they did not know how to cast coin; the cash given by the central state was stored in the treasury and only brought out from time to time to be passed around for admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The country had copper but did not know how to cast coin. Chinese cash sent as gifts was hoarded in the treasury and brought out only occasionally to be admired and passed around.

sentences.zh: 崇寧後，始學鼓鑄，有「海東通寶」、「重寶」、「三韓通寶」三種錢，然其俗不便也。

translations.literal: After Chongning they first learned to cast by drum-furnace; there were three kinds of coin—'Haedong Tongbao,' 'Chongbao,' and 'Samhan Tongbao'—yet their custom found them inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chongning era they learned to cast coin and issued three types: Haedong Tongbao, Chongbao, and Samhan Tongbao. Even so, the people found coin currency awkward.

sentences.zh: 兵器疏簡，無強弩大刀。

translations.literal: Weapons were crude and simple; there were no powerful crossbows or great swords.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms were crude and few. They had no powerful crossbows or great swords.

sentences.zh: 崇尚釋教，雖王子弟亦常一人爲僧。

translations.literal: They revered and upheld Buddhism; even among princes' sons one was commonly made a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism was held in the highest esteem. Even among royal princes it was common for one son to take monastic vows.

sentences.zh: 信鬼，拘陰陽，病不相視，斂不撫棺。

translations.literal: They believed in ghosts, were bound by yin and yang; when ill they did not visit one another, and at burial they did not touch the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: They believed in ghosts and were ruled by yin-yang taboos. The sick did not visit one another, and at funerals mourners did not touch the coffin.

sentences.zh: 貧者死，則露置中野。

translations.literal: When the poor died, the body was exposed and set in the open wild.
translations.idiomatic: When the poor died, the corpse was left exposed in the open countryside.

sentences.zh: 歲以建子月祭天。

translations.literal: Each year in the jianzi month they sacrificed to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Each year they offered sacrifice to Heaven in the first month of the calendar.

sentences.zh: 國東有穴，號礻遂神，常以十月望日迎祭，謂之八關齋，禮儀甚盛，王與妃嬪登樓，大張樂宴飲。

translations.literal: East of the state there was a cave, titled the Suishén; on the fifteenth day of the tenth month they regularly welcomed it for sacrifice, called the Eight Passes Fast—rites very grand, the king and consorts ascended a tower, music spread wide, feasting and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: East of the realm stood a sacred cave dedicated to the Suishén. On the fifteenth day of the tenth month the court welcomed the deity in a grand rite called the Eight Passes Fast. The ceremonies were magnificent: the king and his consorts mounted a tower while music filled the air and feasting ran late into the night.

sentences.zh: 賈人曳羅爲幕，至百匹相聯以示富。

translations.literal: Merchants dragged silk gauze as curtains, linking as many as a hundred bolts to display wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants trailed silk curtains behind them, sometimes linking a hundred bolts together to display their wealth.

sentences.zh: 三歲大祭祠，遍其封內，因是斂民財，而王與諸臣分取之。

translations.literal: Every three years a great sacrifice was held throughout the realm; by this the people's wealth was gathered, and the king and his ministers divided and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years a great sacrifice swept the entire kingdom. The occasion became a levy on the people's wealth, which the king and his ministers then divided among themselves.

sentences.zh: 祖廟在國門之外，大祭則具車服冕圭親祠。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple stood outside the state gate; at the great sacrifice the full chariot, robes, cap, and jade tablet were prepared and the king personally sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple lay outside the capital gate. For the great sacrifice the king donned full regalia with chariot, robes, crown, and jade tablet and performed the rites in person.

sentences.zh: 王城有佛寺七十區而無道觀，大觀中，朝廷遣道士往，乃立福源院，置羽流十餘輩。

translations.literal: In the royal city were seventy Buddhist monasteries and no Daoist abbeys; in the Daguan period the court sent Daoist priests there, and then Fuyuan Cloister was established, with more than ten Daoist clergy placed.
translations.idiomatic: The capital held seventy Buddhist monasteries but no Daoist temples. During the Daguan era the Song court sent Daoist priests to Goryeo, and the Fuyuan Cloister was founded with a dozen ordained Daoists in residence.

sentences.zh: 俗不知醫，自王俁來請醫，後始有通其術者。

translations.literal: The custom did not know medicine; from King U onward physicians were invited, and only afterward were there men who mastered the art.
translations.idiomatic: The people knew nothing of medicine. Beginning with King U, physicians were invited from abroad, and only then did some locals learn the art.

sentences.zh: 人首無枕骨，背扁側。

translations.literal: Human heads lacked occipital bone; the back was flat and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Their skulls lacked a pronounced occipital bone, and their backs were flat and narrow.

sentences.zh: 男子巾幘如唐裝，婦人鬢髻垂右肩，餘發被下，約以絳羅，貫之簪。

translations.literal: Men wore headcloths and kerchiefs like Tang dress; women's temple buns hung over the right shoulder, the remaining hair spread below, bound with crimson silk and pierced with hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore headcloths and kerchiefs in Tang fashion. Women dressed their hair in temple buns draped over the right shoulder, with the rest falling down the back, bound in crimson silk and fastened with pins.

sentences.zh: 旋裙重疊，以多爲勝。

translations.literal: Spiral skirts were layered; having more was considered superior.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore layered spiral skirts, and the more layers one had, the finer the display.

sentences.zh: 男女自爲夫婦者不禁，夏月同川而浴。

translations.literal: Men and women who made themselves husband and wife were not forbidden; in summer months they bathed together in the same stream.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women who paired off on their own were not forbidden. In summer they bathed together in the rivers.

sentences.zh: 婦人、僧、尼皆男子拜。

translations.literal: Women, monks, and nuns were all bowed to by men.
translations.idiomatic: Men bowed to women, monks, and nuns alike.

sentences.zh: 樂聲甚下，無金石之音。

translations.literal: Musical sound was very low; there was no metal or stone tone.
translations.idiomatic: Their music ran very low in pitch and lacked metal or stone instruments.

sentences.zh: 既賜樂，乃分爲左、右二部：左曰唐樂，中國之音也；

translations.literal: After music was bestowed, it was divided into left and right two sections: the left was called Tang music, the sounds of the central state;
translations.idiomatic: After the Song court granted musical instruments, the repertoire was divided into left and right sections. The left was called Tang music—the sounds of China;

sentences.zh: 右曰鄉樂，其故習也。

translations.literal: the right was called village music, their former custom.
translations.idiomatic: the right was called village music, their native tradition.

sentences.zh: 堂上設席，升必脫屨，見尊者則膝行，必跪，應必唯。

translations.literal: In the hall mats were set; ascending one must remove sandals; seeing a superior one knee-walked, must kneel, and in reply must say 'wei.'
translations.idiomatic: Mats were laid in the hall. One removed sandals before stepping up. Before a superior one crawled on the knees, always knelt, and answered every call with 'yes, my lord.'

sentences.zh: 其拜無不答，子拜，父猶半答其禮。

translations.literal: Their bows had none unanswered; when a son bowed, the father still half-returned the rite.
translations.idiomatic: No bow went unanswered. When a son bowed, his father still returned half the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 性仁柔惡殺，不屠宰，欲食羊豕則包以蒿而燔之。

translations.literal: By nature gentle and soft, hating killing, they did not slaughter; if they wished to eat mutton or pork they wrapped it in mugwort and roasted it.
translations.idiomatic: By nature they were gentle and loathed killing. They did not slaughter animals. When they wanted mutton or pork, they wrapped the meat in mugwort and roasted it whole.

sentences.zh: 刑無慘酷之科，唯惡逆及罵父母者斬，餘皆杖肋。

translations.literal: Punishments had no cruel and severe statutes; only treason and reviling parents were beheaded, the rest all flogged on the ribs.
translations.idiomatic: The penal code held no cruel torments. Only treason and cursing one's parents carried beheading. All other offenses were punished by flogging the ribs.

sentences.zh: 外郡刑殺悉送王城，歲以八月減囚死罪，貸流諸島，累赦，視輕重原之。

translations.literal: Executions in outer commanderies were all sent to the royal city; each year in the eighth month prisoners' death sentences were reduced, exiled to the various isles, with repeated amnesties according to severity pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Executions in outlying districts were all sent to the capital. Each year in the eighth month death sentences were commuted and offenders exiled to the islands. Repeated amnesties pardoned crimes according to their severity.

sentences.zh: 自明州定海遇便風，三日入洋，又五日抵墨山，入其境。

translations.literal: From Mingzhou Dinghai, meeting a fair wind, in three days one entered the ocean, and in five more reached Ink Mountain, entering their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Sailing from Dinghai in Mingzhou with a fair wind, one reached the open sea in three days and Ink Mountain five days later, entering Goryeo territory.

sentences.zh: 自墨山過島嶼，詰曲礁石間，舟行甚駛，七日至禮成江。

translations.literal: From Ink Mountain passing islets, winding among reefs, the boat went very swiftly—seven days to the Rites-Complete River.
translations.idiomatic: From Ink Mountain the route threaded among islands and winding reefs, and the ship ran very fast. In seven days one reached the Rites-Complete River.

sentences.zh: 江居兩山間，束以石峽，湍激而下，所謂急水門，最爲險惡。

translations.literal: The river lay between two mountains, constricted by a stone gorge, rapids rushing down—what was called the Urgent Water Gate, most perilous and dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: The river ran between two mountains, narrowed by a stone gorge where the current rushed down—the place called the Urgent Water Gate, the most dangerous stretch of all.

sentences.zh: 又三日抵岸，有館曰碧瀾亭，使人由此登陸，崎嶇山谷四十餘里，乃其國都云。

translations.literal: Three more days and one reached shore; there was a lodge called Bilan Pavilion—envoys from here went ashore, rugged mountains and valleys for more than forty li, and then it was the state capital.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the ship reached shore. There stood the Bilan Pavilion lodge, where envoys went ashore and traveled more than forty li through rugged mountain valleys before reaching the capital—thus ended the sea road to Goryeo.
